On today’s surprisingly affordable edition of Quick Charge, we check out all the latest cheap tricks trucks coming for your hard-earned money in 2027, and challenge the seemingly popular idea that low tech automatically begets low costs.

In a recent development, name for Ransom E. Olds, the guy who founded Oldsmobile in the early part of the last century, cheap truck startup REO is hoping to undercut Jeff Bezos-backed startup Slate by offering a low-tech, low-cost ICE pickup with standard 4WD, a 500,000 usable mile engine life, an open source service solution, and a price that’s nearly $3,000 lower than Slate’s.

If REO can make it happen, it’ll be a seriously impressive accomplishment. That noted, I feel like I’ve seen this episode before – and it was called Elio Motors. Give this one a listen and let us know what you think in the comments.

A small relatively efficient gas truck wouldn't be the worse thing in the world if it gets a couple of those cranky men who associate truck ownership with their virility to buy one instead of a full sized truck that they use to commute to work or to the grocery store and back but I can pretty confidently say it won't come from this guy.

Bitwise XRP ETF Averages $14 Million in Daily Trading in Year One

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (412 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Bitwise XRP ETF traded an average of about $14 million a day over its first year on the market, resulting in over $3.5 billion in total trading volume, according to Bitwise.
  • In a post on X commemorating the Bitwise XRP ETF's first anniversary, Bitwise said the fund had recorded over $667 million in net inflows and had more than $376 million in assets under management (AUM) since launch.
  • Bitwise's XRP ETF started trading on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Bitwise XRP ETF traded an average of about $14 million a day over its first year on the market, resulting in over $3.5 billion in total trading volume, according to Bitwise.

In a post on X commemorating the Bitwise XRP ETF's first anniversary, Bitwise said the fund had recorded over $667 million in net inflows and had more than $376 million in assets under management (AUM) since launch.

Bitwise's XRP ETF started trading on Nov. 20, 2025, on NYSE Arca. It trades under the same ticker as the cryptocurrency it holds, XRP.

Investors can use the ETF's shares to track the price of the token through their brokerage accounts. The fund holds the XRP on behalf of investors. At launch, the ETF charged a 0.34% annual management fee. It also offered a fee waiver for the first $500 million in assets for the first month.

Recent findings suggest that the $3.5 billion in trading volume is the total value of purchases and sales of the ETF's shares. This means the same ETF shares could trade repeatedly. If an investor sells their shares to another investor, that transaction increases trading volume. But the total XRP held in the fund doesn't change in that case.

On the other hand, the $667 million in net inflows represents the total dollar value of latest shares issued over the past year minus redeemed shares.

In a recent development, AUM represents the total dollar value of a fund's assets at a specific moment. Since the fund's total assets are valued in dollars, AUM can fall below cumulative net inflows if the price of XRP declines, even as investors continue to put money into the fund.

The quarterly report filed by Bitwise with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) shows the impact of investor demand and XRP's price on the fund over the past year.

The net asset value of the fund increased from $299.1 million at the end of June to $614.9 million at the end of September.

According to recent reports, over $315.7 million was added to the fund's net assets during that quarter. Just over half of that $315.7 million came from newly introduced share creations.

The fund issued latest shares with a total dollar value of $210.7 million. It also redeemed $32.8 million in shares during that quarter. So that left about $178 million in net new creations.

The fund issued 13.75 million shares and redeemed 2.42 million shares.

#122518. Breaking: Tesla needs wireless charging fast, or its $30,000 Cybercab can’t charge at home

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1416 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Tesla needs wireless charging fast, or its $30,000 Cybercab can’t charge at home

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1416 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is now taking orders for the $29,990 Cybercab, with the first deliveries expected in Austin next month.
  • It has been revealed that the Cybercab has no onboard charger, so it only takes DC fast charging.
  • When Tesla unveiled the Cybercab in 2024, Elon Musk noted it wouldn’t even have a plug.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is now taking orders for the $29,990 Cybercab, with the first deliveries expected in Austin next month. But there’s a problem buyers should know about: they won’t be able to charge it at home.

It has been revealed that the Cybercab has no onboard charger, so it only takes DC fast charging. And the wireless home charging pad Tesla has been teasing since 2023 still isn’t something you can buy.

When Tesla unveiled the Cybercab in 2024, Elon Musk noted it wouldn’t even have a plug. “It just goes over the inductive charger and charges,” he said on stage.

In a recent development, that plan didn’t survive production, or at least the current version in production. Cybercabs have a NACS charge port behind a panel in the rear bumper, and Tesla has been plugging Cybercabs into regular Superchargers in Austin since they joined the fleet.

According to recent reports, the bigger issue is what sits behind that port. Tesla confirmed to attendees at Tesla’s Austin launch event in September that Cybercab has no onboard charger, the box that turns the AC power coming out of your wall into DC power the battery can store.

In a recent development, no onboard charger means no Wall Connector. No Mobile Connector on a 120V outlet, and no Level 2 station at the mall either. If it isn’t a DC fast charger, the Cybercab can’t use it.

In a recent development, for a robotaxi, deleting the onboard charger makes sense. It’s one less part to buy, cool, and carry around, and a fleet car spends its downtime at a depot, not in someone’s garage. Those little things help make the car more economical and efficient.

But Tesla is now selling the Cybercab to individuals.

Sources indicate that as we reported last week, Tesla’s Cybercab autonomy agreement requires a $299 monthly subscription for the car to move at all. The same document puts charging squarely on the buyer: “You are responsible for registration, insurance, parking, charging, general cleaning and all other costs.”.

It also tells owners to “keep the vehicle charged and connected so over-the-air updates can install.” Connected to what, it doesn’t say.

It has been revealed that the Cybercab Order Agreement limits the car to NACS DC fast charging, Superchargers included. It also claims only the registered owner can use the Cybercab, and only while physically present in it for the entire trip.

The subscription agreement carves out one exception: when service is due, the Cybercab “will travel autonomously, unoccupied to a Tesla service center.” Nothing similar exists for charging.

So you can’t send your Cybercab to a Supercharger at 2 a.m. while you sleep, which is the one thing a self-driving car should be great at. You’d have to ride along, sit in a two-seater at a Supercharger while it charges, and ride back home.

The obvious answer is the wireless home charger Tesla keeps promising.

According to recent reports, tesla first demonstrated what looked like a wireless home charging station during its Investor Day in March 2023. Later that year, chief designer Franz von Holzhausen confirmed the project on Jay Leno’s Garage, saying owners would “just drive over the pad in your garage” to start charging.

Tesla then filed patents for the charging pad and, after the Cybercab unveiling, released a video of it charging the robotaxi at 25 kW, claiming efficiency “well above 90%.” In February, the FCC granted Tesla a waiver to use ultra-wideband radios to guide the Cybercab onto the pad.

Recent findings suggest that and that’s where it stops. Tesla has never sold the pad, never priced it, and never given it a launch date. It even gave up on wireless charging for the Cybertruck last year, even though the truck shipped with the connectors for it.

With deliveries estimated for December, Tesla has about six weeks to launch a home pad if it wants the first owners to charge in their own garage.

Industry observers note that tesla’s own looks for Cybercab charging revolve around fleet depots. In Austin, it filed plans for a hub on St. Elmo Road with 48 V4 Supercharger stalls in a first phase and cabinets to support 80 wireless chargers in a second.

Tesla could, in theory, let private owners use it. But with the owner-presence rule, that means riding to a depot across town and waiting there. That’s a Supercharger visit with extra steps.

The other route is a home DC charger, and those exist. We covered Sigenergy’s 25 kW bidirectional DC charging module last year, which bypasses a car’s onboard charger the same way a Supercharger does. Lunar Energy also announced a 25 kW home DC charger this year, but it’s not expected until mid-2027.

Sources indicate that neither is a plug-and-play answer. Sigenergy’s module is built to sit inside its SigenStor home battery system, which isn’t cheap, and Tesla would have to support third-party DC charging on a car it controls this tightly. Tesla could also build its own small DC wall unit. It hasn’t announced one, but CEO Elon Musk talked about integrating one into the Powerwall for years.

This is what happens when you take a vehicle designed for a fleet and sell it to consumers to hit a deadline. And let’s be honest, charging is probably not even in the top 5 of problems with selling the Cybercab to personal owners in its current state.

In a recent development, musk promised a Cybercab would be sold to a customer for under $30,000 before 2027. Technically, he’s going to make it. But on the Q3 earnings call, he also remarked “the vast majority” of Cybercabs will stay Tesla-owned and run as transport-as-a-service. The car was clearly engineered around that, and deleting the onboard charger is the best example.

That saved Tesla money on every unit. The cost now lands on the few people buying one.

I don't see any evidence that the production Cybercab has the onboard hardware to use such a pad. Besides the wireless receiver coil it would need some kind of charging hardware to convert the pulsed wireless charging into DC to charge the battery.

If you live in Austin next to a Supercharger, you’ll manage. But think about what Tesla is actually selling here: a self-driving car that can’t drive itself to charge, can’t charge in your garage, and needs you sitting in it at a Supercharger. That’s worse than owning a Model 3 with a Wall Connector, and it costs $299 a month on top.

It has been revealed that the fix exists in Tesla’s labs. It has the pad, the patents, and the FCC approval. It needs to ship it as a product, ideally bundled with the car, or change the contract to let the Cybercab go charge on its own.

Will the first Cybercab owners get a wireless pad in December, or will they spend their evenings at Superchargers? And if it releases, how much will it cost? The rare few home wireless chargers that have been sold to date have been quite expensive, and the value proposition of the Cybercab, which is presently basically a $300 a month lease with a $30,000 down payment, is already pretty awful.

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (504 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • USDT’s market cap may now be a key metric to watch for signs of a market bottom.
  • Recent findings suggest that technically, Tether’s USDT is experiencing its most severe quarterly de-pegging since Q2 2022, which saw over 18% of its market cap drained away, totalling roughly $15 billion.
  • The chart below highlights this trend.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

USDT’s market cap may now be a key metric to watch for signs of a market bottom.

Recent findings suggest that technically, Tether’s USDT is experiencing its most severe quarterly de-pegging since Q2 2022, which saw over 18% of its market cap drained away, totalling roughly $15 billion. Although currently the de-pegging figure is lower (around -5% so far in Q4), the consequence remains impactful. Since 2022, USDT’s market cap has increased to almost $180 billion from approximately $80 billion. This means even a smaller percentage drop now represents a much larger amount of liquidity leaving the market.

The chart below highlights this trend. According to CryptoQuant data, USDT’s market cap has fallen by $8.83 billion over the 60 days leading up to the 22nd of November. Furthermore, its 30-day Moving Average is also falling, which indicates the decline is still in motion.

It has been revealed that to put this into perspective, back in 2022 a 5% fall in Tether’s [USDT] $80 billion market cap would have caused approximately $4 billion worth of liquidity to exit the market. However, when applying the same 5% market cap reduction to today’s $180 billion figure, almost $9 billion is now leaving the market. That’s more than 2x the amount of liquidity being pulled out for the same percentage decline.

In this context, USDT’s growing market cap means its contraction now has a much bigger impact on liquidity.

Tether’s ongoing contraction further adds to the liquidity concerns.

TVL on DeFi platforms has decreased to just over $70 billion. This is from an approximate figure of $140 billion prior to the October 2025 crash. Thus, in just over a year, the TVL on DeFi platforms has almost been cut in half. Coupled with the reduction in USDT’s market cap, this suggests there is poor liquidity and reduced capital involvement within the crypto space.

However, the impact goes beyond DeFi liquidity. As the chart below indicates, the broader crypto market has also experienced a significant bear run. So far in Q4, the market has lost over 28% of its value, reducing the market cap from $2.84 trillion down to below $1.8 trillion, meaning almost $500 billion has been erased. The key takeaway? This is the worst quarterly fall for the crypto market since Q2 2022, which also witnessed the largest-ever de-pegging of Tether’s USDT stablecoin.

According to AMBCrypto, this overlap is not random.

According to recent reports, rather, with Tether’s market cap now much larger than it was in 2022, even a small drop in USDT supply is now having a bigger impact on overall market liquidity. This makes USDT supply an important metric to watch during the current downturn.

Until USDT’s market cap bottoms, a sustained crypto market bottom may remain out of reach.

DeFi TVL has nearly halved to $70 billion, while the broader crypto market is down over 28% in Q4.

USDT’s shrinking market cap points to continued liquidity outflows, making its recovery a key signal to watch for a market bottom.

Coinbase Reveals COIN Buybacks as It Capitalizes on AI

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (399 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: U

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said on X that the tech giant is repurchasing stock in the fourth quarter because investors are overlooking the potential of the payments business for AI agents.
  • "Good to take advantage of market dislocations," said Armstrong.
  • The tech giant is buying back stock using funds previously authorized for repurchases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said on X that the tech giant is repurchasing stock in the fourth quarter because investors are overlooking the potential of the payments business for AI agents.

"Good to take advantage of market dislocations," said Armstrong.

The tech giant is buying back stock using funds previously authorized for repurchases. He didn't specify the number of COIN shares, the price or the amount spent.

At the start of the quarter, Coinbase had $1.96 billion left to repurchase stock. Over the prior three months, it repurchased 37,995 shares for a total cost of $5.3 million, at an average price of $139.91. All repurchases occurred in August, according to its third-quarter report.

In a recent development, coinbase's board of directors initially authorized stock buybacks of up to $1 billion in October 2024. A year later, the buyback authorization was doubled. The tech giant also received an option to repurchase some outstanding debt.

The board increased the buyback limit again in January 2026, bringing the total authorization to $4 billion.

Recent findings suggest that some buybacks have been carried out to cancel stock issued as employee compensation. By the end of September, the organization had repurchased 10.2 million Class A shares and canceled more than 85% of the stock issued for employee compensation since the fourth quarter of 2024. This is according to an earnings presentation.

Armstrong envisions a scenario where crypto and AI are involved in different aspects of the same transaction.

It has been revealed that for example, AI agents might help users make financial decisions and follow their instructions. Then, a crypto network may be used to transfer funds.

Coinbase wants to provide accounts, payment services, and marketplaces for humans and AI agents to use.

"With AI, everybody has a private banker in your pocket that can help you make better financial decisions," Armstrong posted on Nov. 25.

Coinbase added its wallet and payment services to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments. This offers a way for developers to build agents on Amazon and allow the software to discover paid services. Agents can make small payments when necessary.

Now Armstrong is inviting developers to add their specialized AI models to Agentic.Market.

According to Armstrong, an AI agent can choose which specialist to hire for a task based on its capabilities and price. Coinbase provides the platform where agents can find specialists and pay them.

XRP traded at just 29 cents in Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market during a localized sell-off, raising questions about thin liquidity.

XRP reportedly traded at just 29 cents in Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market during a sharp, localized sell-off discussed by crypto commentator Crypto Sensei.

His video examines whether the trades reflected an exchange-specific liquidity problem rather than a broader XRP collapse, alongside falling ledger activity and disputed price forecasts.

According to the account presented in the video, 11 Canadian-dollar markets fell by at least 65%, with bitcoin trading below 18,000 and ether around 560.

The host cites November 20, 2026 as the incident date and reports that Kraken considered the orders correctly processed and would let the trades stand.

It has been revealed that the analyst didn’t include trade records or Kraken’s full statement. Those limits matter: the reported 29-cent execution should not be confused with XRP’s prevailing price across exchanges.

According to recent reports, crypto Sensei attributes the dislocation to heavy selling meeting insufficient liquidity. Buyers may have secured steep discounts, while sellers received prices far below those available elsewhere.

“Whoever sold and just got totally wiped out here, I feel for you,” he states. The video does not establish whether individual losses resulted from discretionary sales, automated orders or liquidations.

A separate headline claiming the XRP Ledger had lost 60% of its users also draws scrutiny.

The underlying figure, according to the clarification cited in the YouTube video, was roughly a 63% decline in daily activity, not evidence that a comparable share of holders permanently departed or sold their XRP.

The host challenges Jake Claver’s repeated $100 year-end XRP forecast, arguing that institutional adoption is a longer process than such targets suggest. He also distinguishes Ripple’s business expansion from confirmed institutional use of XRP itself.

Former Ripple executive and Evernorth CEO Ashish Birla offers a longer-term XRP development case in a clip: Evernorth intends to deploy XRP on-chain, pursue yield and support ecosystem features rather than simply hold the asset. The video leaves the execution details and eventual returns unresolved.

According to recent reports, for HODLers, these are separate questions: whether an exchange has enough liquidity, whether ledger usage is growing, and whether adoption creates demand for XRP. A dramatic trade print, or an ambitious treasury strategy, does not answer all three.

  • This particular change addresses a bug with order-book behavior around “tec” failures, which are failures where the transaction processing is rolled back.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Official XRP Ledger's repository account received a proposed fix to keep only transaction-independent offer removals after a tec that should address the disappearance of failed transactions.

This particular change addresses a bug with order-book behavior around “tec” failures, which are failures where the transaction processing is rolled back. In some circumstances, offers can be removed when a "tec" failure occurs, even though the transaction that triggered it never succeeded.

In a recent development, in one scenario, a trader could have an existing offer removed before they’re able to add a replacement (for instance, if they don’t have enough reserve to add a newly introduced offer). In another, a more complicated Flow could temporarily leave an offer unfunded, only to have funds restored if a subsequent step fails, again resulting in an offer being removed even though the transaction that triggered it failed.

To address this problem, rippled will attempt to remove offers that were marked for removal upon tec failure any time a tec failure occurs. Previously, this was attempted for certain tec error codes but not others, with some additional restrictions around Flow-related offer removals (an offer will only be marked for removal if the owner’s balance has not changed in any relevant ways during the course of the Flow).

Sources indicate that offers that have already expired can still be removed, but offers owned by the transactor will be skipped. This is a best effort to make sure offers are consistently added/removed from the order book and should reduce confusing trade results.

Offers to/from regular XRP accounts and balances, XRP sends are unaffected and there are no proposed API changes.

This does not change XRP supply, fees, transaction capacity, etc. and is unlikely to have any effect on XRPL usage or XRP price (other than maybe making XRPL trading more appealing to traders).

This change would mostly affect traders using decentralized exchanges (DEXs) and particularly those using complex/routed/fill-or-kill orders/self-crosses.

It has been revealed that on November 23, XRP briefly hit $1.026 before dropping below $1. Reports indicate crypto selling in general and ETF outflows have been putting pressure on XRP lately. By November 25, XRP was trading at ~$0.92. This software change would not be a catalyst for a price recovery of XRP.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BitMine, the world’s largest Ethereum [ETH] DAT, has reportedly reached investments (including crypto) worth $11.1 billion as of 23rd November.

Recent findings suggest that according to a recent update, the company now holds 6,085,564 ETH, valued at approximately $10.4 billion at $1,713 per token, along with 216 Bitcoin [BTC]. This, after BitMine purchased 7,819 ETH over the past week.

Meanwhile, the tech giant has staked 5.22 million ETH, representing approximately 86% of its holdings. BitMine estimates that its current staked holdings could generate $245 million in annualized revenue, potentially rising to $286 million once all its ETH is staked.

At the same time, SharpLink repurchased $10 million worth of its own shares (SBET), signalling its confidence in the firm’s long-term strategy and its current valuation.

According to recent reports, for SharpLink, the move is also linked to its Ethereum treasury strategy. The company aims to increase its ETH per share, which measures how much Ethereum backs each outstanding company share.

By reducing the number of shares in circulation through buybacks, SharpLink can potentially increase this metric without purchasing additional ETH.

These accumulation strategies coincided with ETH’s price trading at $1,692.78 following a drop of 1.9% at press time.

Despite a drop below the $2K price level, however, crypto analyst Michaël van de Poppe pointed out that Ethereum’s performance against Bitcoin has remained relatively stable. In fact, over the past two weeks, Bitcoin saw a sharp 25% decline.

That’s a sign of strength, as generally, markets would be absolutely collapsing when it comes to altcoins vs. Bitcoin.

This is noteworthy because altcoins typically suffer heavier losses than Bitcoin during market downturns as investors move towards relatively safer assets. ETH’s ability to hold its ground against BTC could therefore indicate improving relative strength and potentially growing investor interest.

Van de Poppe also claimed that Ethereum may be approaching a possible trend reversal. For this to happen, the ETH/BTC trading pair needs to break above the 0.0290 level and reclaim its 21-day moving average.

Echoing similar sentiments, another analyst noted that Bitcoin has been trading within a nine-month range and recently recorded a lower low, raising concerns about further downside.

According to recent reports, ethereum, meanwhile, recovered from its June bottom, rallied by approximately 86%, and subsequently held above its previous low of $1,506. This might allude to a potential higher-low formation for ETH, hinting at an improving market structure.

All in all, Bitcoin is still struggling to establish a convincing bottom, while Ethereum has been showing signs of relative strength. However, ETH needs to break key resistance levels before a sustained uptrend can be confirmed.

Industry observers note that here, it’s worth noting that Ethereum’s Taker Buy/Sell Ratio has remained largely below 1 throughout November 2026, indicating that aggressive selling volume exceeded aggressive buying volume across exchanges. At press time, the ratio stood at 0.98, hinting at sustained selling pressure and relatively weak buying demand.

In a recent development, additionally, CoinShares recently sold its entire Ethereum holdings in October, generating $19.3 million. Given that it will use these millions to repurchase its own shares under a $40 million buyback program, caution makes sense.

Dogecoin co-founder Billy Markus, who is known on X as Shibetoshi Nakamoto, has explained why, in his opinion, no one can predict the prices of cryptocurrencies.

Markus shared his opinion on Wednesday in a reply to an X post with a prediction that the price of Zcash (ZEC) would fall to $100.

"my opinion is that every single cryptocurrency has an arbitrary value mostly unrelated to anything except that people believe they can make more money if others buy it from them in the future and thus all future projections are pissing in the wind," the Dogecoin co-founder wrote.

Markus did not mention Zcash or any other token by name in his reply, and his post was about every single cryptocurrency on the market, including the one he created himself.

my opinion is that every single cryptocurrency has an arbitrary value mostly unrelated to anything except people believe they can make more money if others buy it from them in the future and thus all future projections are pissing in the wind.

At the time of the post, ZEC was trading at around $728, up by 41.3% over the past year, according to price data on X.

In a recent development, the latest comment from Markus comes a week after Bitwise filed an S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a spot Zcash ETF. According to the filing, the fund is set to trade on the Texas Stock Exchange under the ticker ZEC, and it will not stake ZEC or use shielded transactions.

Industry observers note that markus created Dogecoin together with Jackson Palmer in December 2013. The two developers based the cryptocurrency on the Doge meme with a Shiba Inu dog, and they rolled out it as a joke about the crypto market of that time.

Industry observers note that markus has stated in the past that it took him a couple of hours to write the code of Dogecoin. In 2021, Markus also said on X that he had sold all of his DOGE in 2015 after he lost his job, and that he got about the price of a used Honda Civic for it.

Since then, Markus has stayed active on X under the Shibetoshi Nakamoto name, and he often replies to posts about crypto prices, forecasts and fresh tokens.

In June 2022, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates spoke about crypto and NFTs at the TechCrunch Sessions: Climate conference.

"As an asset class, it's 100% based on the greater fool theory — that somebody's going to pay more for it than I do," Gates noted.

Earlier, at the Berkshire Hathaway annual meeting in April 2022, Warren Buffett said that he would not buy all of the Bitcoin in the world even for $25.

"If you told me you own all of the bitcoin in the world and you offered it to me for $25, I wouldn't take it because what would I do with it?" Buffett remarked.

According to recent reports, according to Buffett, Bitcoin does not produce anything. At the same meeting, Buffett compared it with farmland and apartment buildings, and he said that he would pay for a share of them because farmland produces food and apartments produce rent.

Combined with Bitcoin and Ethereum weakness, the crypto markets stalled, helping establish a BNB correction back to the $537 swing low and potentially toward $500.

Technically, the swing structure was bullish and will remain so until a weekly BNB close below $500.

It has been revealed that zooming in, we find a bearish BNB structure. The fair value gap (red box) from $551.45-$576.39 was swept, helped by Monday’s volatility. Failure to break beyond $600 cemented the bears’ dominance.

An hourly session close above $562.19 would invalidate this sell setup, while the $503 and $500 remain feasible targets.

Bitcoin's long-term trend value, based on various models like "Proposal B", has been set ridiculously high, so chasing targets set by those models might not be the best decision out there, considering modern market conditions.

A revised Bitcoin Power Law model sets BTC's long-term price at $99,000, which is almost $50,000 below the $146,725 estimate that has been used by the traditional Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) model.

The creator of the newer, accordingly more accurate model believes the Bitcoin Power Law is still valid, but the fair value is certainly nowhere near the relevant market conditions.

One way or another, the newer models still set the current price threshold at one of the lowest historical levels in the history of the asset—approximately the 1st percentile of its distribution, which means that it stands among 60 of Bitcoin's daily closes that fell below this threshold.

Industry observers note that the new model uses a completely different method for calculation: Quantile Regression instead of Ordinary Least Squares (OLS). The main difference is that OLS guesses Bitcoin's price trend based on its historical averages, while QR uses specific points in the price distribution, not an average. Essentially, the newer calculation model smoothens out extremes that made OLS less accurate.

Despite the newer calculation and estimation approach, the improved calculation algorithm and everything else, models are estimating, not making solid predictions.

There are thousands of other factors to consider when determining Bitcoin's next move, so any kind of model is useful only for evaluating the momentum and historical significance of the most recent movements.

Recent findings suggest that the model also places its 0.1 percentile at $55,185, a level below which Bitcoin has closed only six times. The creator argues that only the lower part of Bitcoin's price distribution, between the 0.1 and 5th percentiles, may continue following the Power Law, while higher levels gradually move down towards this lower boundary.

The model also uses Protocol Time instead of Calendar Time. Still, its creator maintains that the Power Law is not broken. The problem, according to this view, is how previous models measured it and how much they allowed market bubbles to influence the results.

The ID. Polo GTI “brings the legendary GTI driving pleasure into the electric future,” VW mentioned after opening pre-orders last month.

Volkswagen previewed a mysterious upcoming hot hatch draped under a cloth that appears to be a souped-up version of the ID. Polo GTI. Despite its attempt to “hide” it, you can see the massive rear wing and wide wheel arches under the cloth.

The tech giant promised that “something really spicy” will be served this Friday, November 20, with the tags #Volkswagen, #GTI, and #GTI50.

A post shared by Volkswagen (@volkswagen).

Volkswagen’s head of driving dynamics, Florian Umbach, told Autocar earlier this year that the tech giant is planning to launch the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, a more powerful variant that will deliver close to 300 hp, up from 223 hp in the standard model.

Umbach remarked that Volkswagen is developing “a similar kind of paddleshift power delivery that the Hyundai N cars have” for the upcoming electric hot hatch.

Recent findings suggest that hyundai’s performance EVs, the IONIQ 5 N and IONIQ 6 N, feature a simulated gear-shifting system called N e-Shift that uses paddle shifters on the steering wheel to replicate the feel of an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission. In a recent development, it has yet to be confirmed whether the hot hatch debuting on Friday is, in fact, the new ID. Polo Clubsport, but the design clues give us a good idea of what’s coming.

According to recent reports, man, $45k for a starting price is a little uncomfortably steep for a hatch, given there are a little bigger options in that range. I wish it started somewhere in the 30s to be competitive.

Check back on Friday for the full details.

Volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000).

Like the first Golf GTI from 1976, the electric ID. Polo GTI uses a front-wheel-drive powertrain. The front-mounted electric motor delivers 223 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft (290 Nm) of instant torque, enabling it to sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 6.8 seconds.

In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI, the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

  • Issuers must have FSC approval and at least 5 billion won in equity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The South Korean FSC’s upcoming draft bill could change things for the country’s crypto space. What’s what’s going on exactly?

Under the newly introduced strategy, banks put together can own more than half of any won stablecoin issuer. A fintech company can still be the largest shareholder, but they can’t run the show alone anymore.

Issuers must have FSC approval and at least 5 billion won in equity. Reserves must cover 100% of tokens in circulation, and holders must be able to cash out at face value right away.

Recent findings suggest that as far as exchanges go, one shareholder can hold 20% or 34% with FSC approval. They’ll also need separate licences for dealing, brokerage, and custody.

But… domestic ICOs would be legal again.

According to recent reports, south Korea’s plan is a 22% tax on crypto gains above 2.5 million won a year. It was meant to kick in this January, but it looks like that date’s been pushed back to 2029.

One reason is that it’s the earliest Korea can start swapping crypto tax data with the United States.

If that happens, it won’t be the first delay. The tax was first proposed back in 2020 and has been shelved several times since.

In a recent development, enforcement is still active though. AMBCrypto previously reported that 27 unlicensed exchange websites were blocked recently, including KuCoin, MEXC and BingX. This was after their apps were already restricted.

Users on those platforms are being nudged towards the country’s 28 licensed exchanges.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Praxis, a cryptography preprint cleared for posting on Nov.
  • Imagine moving Bitcoin through a bridge.
  • According to recent reports, to get the Bitcoin back, you would give up that claim.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Praxis, a cryptography preprint cleared for posting on Nov. 23, proposes a way that could make it easier to test Bitcoin payments by reducing both the size of data locked behind a proof and the computing work needed to encrypt it.

Imagine moving Bitcoin through a bridge. The bridge locks the coins on the Bitcoin mainnet while you hold a matching claim on another chain.

According to recent reports, to get the Bitcoin back, you would give up that claim. The bridge then needs to release the right amount to the right recipient. A design using witness encryption could make the proof that you gave up the claim unlock the information needed to authorize the payment.

In the Praxis preprint, David Tse, Nikhil Vanjani and Psi Vesely described how to set a condition for opening encrypted information.

In their example, someone with a valid mathematical proof that the condition is met can recover the key that opens the encrypted data. The authors list bridges without a custodian and rules about how Bitcoin can be spent as possible applications.

According to recent reports, bitcoin already checks conditions when someone spends coins. One familiar condition is a valid signature showing that the spender controls the right key. Checking a compact proof of a complicated calculation directly on Bitcoin is harder because its scripting language gives developers a limited set of on-chain checks.

It has been revealed that an earlier proposal, Bitcoin PIPEs v2, encrypts a Bitcoin signing key behind a condition. A valid proof unlocks the signing key outside the Bitcoin network, and the resulting transaction carries a signature Bitcoin already knows how to check.

The earlier PIPEs v2 proposal shows where a proof and a signature would each do their work.

A bridge would have to tie the proof and the resulting signing authority to the intended recipient and amount.

In the article’s bridge example, the proof would show that the claim on the other network had been retired.

Industry observers note that illustrative sequence based on PIPEs v2 and Bitcoin's existing signature validation. Praxis is a separate preprint about the underlying type of encryption.

In the article’s bridge example, the proof would show that the claim on the other network had been retired.

Recent findings suggest that in the example, the proof would establish that the matching claim had been retired. Bitcoin would see a signature, so the bridge would have to make sure the signing authority applies to the intended payment, including the recipient and amount.

The encryption scheme lets designers tie access to a proof, and turning that into a working withdrawal system is a separate job.

Industry observers note that earlier BABE research uses witness encryption for one specific kind of mathematical check. Praxis is designed for a much wider range of conditions, as long as a solution to the condition can be checked efficiently.

That opens up more designs researchers could test without asking Bitcoin to do the complicated proof check itself.

In the paper's example, the authors calculate that the encrypted package would take up 7.88 GiB at their stated 100-bit security level.

For the same condition, key length and stated security level, they estimate that the package size and the work of encrypting it are each below one ten-billionth of the costs they calculate for earlier designs by Hair and Sahai.

Sources indicate that the authors compared calculated sizes and operation counts across schemes with different security assumptions. Anyone opening the Praxis package would still need access to several gigabytes of encrypted data.

Recent findings suggest that the authors count the work of opening the package from the point when a valid proof is already available. A bridge using this approach would also have to account for the time and computing power needed to produce that proof, wherever it is produced.

It has been revealed that the proof system used in the example also needs an honestly run setup. The authors say anyone who kept the setup secret could make proofs that pass the check and open packages tied to that setup.

A team building a bridge would have to handle that risk as well as the logistics of producing proofs and making the encrypted package available when someone needs to withdraw.

Ripple has once again landed a major partnership in Türkiye, but this time around with one of the country’s largest private banks, putting XRP in the spotlight.

While this comes as part of Ripple’s growing expansion into the traditional financial space, the blockchain firm revealed it has partnered with Yapı Kredi, a major Turkish private bank, to support its cryptocurrency business.

As part of the partnership agreement, Ripple Custody will help the bank to securely manage its digital assets and provide custody services for its crypto trading platform dubbed Yapı Kredi Kripto.

While the partnership demands the full integration of the Ripple custodial infrastructure, the firm revealed that Ripple Custody will be installed on the bank's own premises.

This way, Yapı Kredi will have access to adequate security and control it needs to manage all digital assets on behalf of its customers, boosting its security.

The development is significant for the bank and the broader Turkish crypto market; it also marks a major milestone for Ripple as the firm claims to be the only custody service provider currently supporting leading Turkish banks licensed by the CMB as crypto asset custodians.

It is crucial to note that Türkiye currently stands as one of the world's top 10 retail crypto markets, with XRP recorded as one of its most widely used cryptocurrencies.

With Yapı Kredi now fortifying its position as a major player in Türkiye’s fast-growing crypto market, its partnership with the blockchain firm associated with XRP is likely to open upcoming opportunities for XRP while positioning it for bigger adoption in the country.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, decentralised exchanges, or DEXs, use smart contracts or liquidity pools to facilitate cryptocurrency trading. Customers are at the core of DEXs, as they retain complete control over their assets and do not need to depend on centralized exchanges to protect their funds or process their withdrawals. DEXs let users maintain ownership of their private keys and also reduce the risk of custody failures.

Here is our list of the top 8 decentralized exchanges in the space that people can trade on:.

Pancake or PancakeSwap is one of the most popular DEXs on the BNB Chain and was created to provide users with a low-cost, accessible alternative to Ethereum-based decentralized exchanges.

The platform recently rebranded from PancakeSwap to Pancake, dropping “Swap” as it expanded from a single-chain token-swap DEX to a multi-chain liquidity hub spanning 11+ blockchains, and added perpetual futures and 24/7 tokenized stocks and ETFs.

Uniswap introduced the Automated Market Maker (AMM) model that changed how cryptocurrency trading could take place without any central intermediaries or traditional order books. People could swap tokens directly from their wallets across Ethereum and other blockchains.

The platform also allows customers to earn rewards through peer-to-peer trading, and the open-source architecture has influenced others in the space, making it an key reference point for the DEX industry.

Raydium leverages Solana’s high-speed blockchain infrastructure, combining AMM, liquidity infrastructure, and token trading functionality. This is useful not just for DeFi people but also for retail users.

Recent findings suggest that customers can trade and exchange their assets directly through their wallets. The tools on Raydium help fresh projects establish liquidity and attract traders. RAY is the native token of the platform and is useful with governance and incentives on the platform.

It has been revealed that hyperliquid has an order book that runs on-chain instead of an AMM, giving users a centralized experience. The platform is especially known for its perpetual futures and spot trading services, whereas the ecosystem itself supports borrowing, lending, and real-world assets.

According to recent reports, the platform is a Layer 1 chain and consists of 2 main components: HyperCore and HyperEVM. HyperBFT is the consensus mechanism used underneath to support both. Stop, limit, and margin orders are all supported on Hyperliquid. HYPE is the native token of the platform.

Balancer is a DEX protocol built on Ethereum that supports multi-token liquidity pools and yield-bearing assets. Token pairings can be customized with multiple assets, unlike the traditional 50/50 pairings. It functions more like an automated portfolio manager, customizing token weights, creating pools with adjustable weight ratios, and letting users set their own trading fee.

The platform provides a level of flexibility that lets customers and liquidity providers create specialized trading environments and program them as per their needs.

SushiSwap was launched as a fork of Uniswap in 2020 and lets consumers trade through liquidity pools instead of traditional order books. These users can either be Traders or Swappers or users who want to exchange one cryptocurrency for another; or Liquidity Providers who supply assets to liquidity pools to conduct trades.

The platform uses a multichain approach and supports various blockchain networks, letting customers access different DeFi environments. The native token of the platform is SUSHI, which is useful in governance and incentive-based applications.

Recent findings suggest that orca lets customers swap and conduct transactions at lightning fast speeds. Whirlpools are the platform’s concentrated liquidity pools that let liquidity providers provide capital within selected price ranges instead of distributing it uniformly across a price curve.

In a recent development, orca is the native token of the platform. The platform’s simple interface appeals to a lot of traders. Wallet-to-wallet trading of SPL tokens is also a viable option for people.

Sources indicate that meteora is a liquidity protocol built on Solana focusing on providing advanced liquidity management and supporting token swaps. Dynamic Liquidity Market Maker or DLMM is a major feature of the platform allowing liquidity providers to allocate assets across different price bins.

Liquidity providers get to concentrate their assets around selected trading prices and various liquidity pool configurations can accomodate various market conditions and trading strategies. Meteora also supports emerging token projects and liquidity tools that can be helpful to establish trading markets and manage liquidity.

Decentralised exchanges are an essential part of the crypto and DeFi ecosystem. DEX platforms give consumers an extra level of control over their assets when they buy, sell, exchange or manage their assets.

While every trader has their own requirements, the best platform would depend upon individual needs, preferred networks, trading pairs and risks. Owners should do their own research before investing.

The Shiba Inu ecosystem may be set for a privacy boost, as longtime SHIB community member and developer Mazrael hints at privacy potential coming to the blockchain.

Shiba Inu's privacy potential draws from Oxbow's Privacy Pools, the privacy design coauthored by Ethereum cofounder Vitalik Buterin, which is presently a plug-in in the Ethereum Foundation's Kohaku wallet SDK.Mazrael noted that Shibarium is now ready for Oxbow's Privacy Pools, with the groundwork already being done.

According to recent reports, WOOF 🐶🪖🫡 And it's privacy done the regulation-friendly way. Privacy Pools come from a 2023 paper Vitalik co-wrote: deposits are screened, so stolen funds can't hide in the crowd, while honest users stay private. No KYC, no backdoors, and you can always exit publicly. Two ways to bring it to Shibarium: 0xbow deploys it themselves, or the community deploys the same contracts and runs a relayer. Shibarium is ready either way, and ShibWallet already runs it on testnet 🔥.

The groundwork done on Shibarium (Chain ID 109) includes Cancun opcodes, BN254 pairing support for zero-knowledge proofs, CreateX and Arachnid factories and verified PoseidonT3 and PoseidonT4 contracts at Ethereum addresses.

Mazrael shared a GitHub document, "Shibarium (chain 109) support: chain is prepared," which highlighted this fact. Addressed to the Oxbow team was a request: "Hi 0xbow team! We build on Shibarium (chain ID 109) and would love to see Privacy Pools there. We've done the groundwork so a deployment would be as easy as possible, and ShibWallet plans to integrate it through Kohaku from day one.".

Mazrael explained that Privacy Pools originated from a 2023 paper Ethereum cofounder Vitalik coauthored: deposits are screened, so stolen funds can't hide in the crowd, while honest owners stay private. No KYC, no backdoors and users can always exit publicly.

Two ways to bring it to Shibarium include 0xbow deploys it themselves, or the community deploys the same contracts and runs a relayer.

For the first option, Mazrael has relayed a GitHub request to the Oxbow team, which is at the moment showing signs of a green light, with Mazrael remarking that "they did the approval thing when we posted basically.".

According to recent reports, A 0xbow privacy pool deployment for Shiba Inu will bring 'entry point', 'verifiers', and 'PrivacyPoolSimple' for native BONE (Shibarium's gas token). It will also bring 'PrivacyPoolComplex' for SHIB and other ecosystem tokens later.

The Shib ecosystem would become privacy-complian and ShibWallet would integrate it through Kohaku from day one.

According to recent reports, chainflip Labs remarked the cross-chain exchange had begun returning available balances to liquidity providers on five networks after the Nov. 21 theft from its Bitcoin and Ethereum vaults.

Chainflip Labs noted in its Nov. 23 incident report that it had initiated the returns as a precaution on Solana, Arbitrum, Tron, BNB Chain and Polkadot Asset Hub. The report provided no list of refund transactions or total amount that had reached wallets.

The returns cover assets that were free in providers’ accounts. Assets committed to open lending, strategy or range-order positions may still be in those accounts, Labs remarked.

A provider with both types of balances could receive a transfer at the designated wallet and still have capital committed to an open position.

The money that arrives in the wallet comes from the part of that provider’s account eligible for this return. A range order, for example, uses assets from the provider’s balance to supply liquidity within a set price range.

Chainflip had paused swaps, deposits, and withdrawals by 8:31 a.m. UTC on Nov. 21. All three remained paused when Labs issued the report. Chainflip’s homepage still displayed a service outage notice on Nov. 24, and the report gave no reopening date.

Sources indicate that the postmortem put the Bitcoin loss at about 133.34 BTC across two withdrawals on Nov. 21.

It has been revealed that labs stated the Ethereum vault lost about 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT. The team valued the combined losses from the two vaults at about $12.6 million using prices from the morning of Nov. 21.

The estimate puts the Bitcoin, Ethereum, and stablecoin losses on the same dollar basis at the time of the theft.

Industry observers note that the stolen Bitcoin remained at two identified addresses as of 4:18 p.m. UTC on Nov. 23, Labs said. The team said it had brought in ZeroShadow to help trace and recover stolen funds.

Chainflip Labs was still determining which customers were affected by the theft and how much each had lost. The team said its follow-up would cover the recovery initiative and how it would treat affected users.

The team discussed incentives and financing as ways to recapitalize its most active liquidity providers and help restore service.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Compare the top hardware and software crypto wallets to find your safest, easiest self-custody setup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Cryptopedia » Best Crypto Wallets: Top 7 Picks for Max Security and Ease of Use.

Compare the top hardware and software crypto wallets to find your safest, easiest self-custody setup.

Sources indicate that keeping your cryptocurrency on an exchange is convenient, but it comes with risks. If the exchange gets hacked, freezes withdrawals, or runs into financial trouble, accessing your funds can become difficult. Using a self-custody wallet gives you direct control over your private keys and, ultimately, your crypto.

Whether you are holding Bitcoin for the next decade, trading memecoins on Solana, or exploring decentralized finance (DeFi), choosing the right wallet matters. Some wallets are designed to keep your assets as secure as possible, while others make it easier to trade, manage tokens, and connect to Web3 apps.

To help you find the right option, we’ve put together a list of seven popular crypto wallets, covering what each one does best, its main advantages, and what to consider before choosing it.

*Prices change frequently, so always confirm on the manufacturer’s official website.

If your primary goal is long-term wealth preservation, Ledger remains the industry benchmark for cold storage.

Unlike mobile apps that stay connected to the internet, Ledger devices store your private keys inside an offline, certified Secure Element chip, the same class of chip used in passports and credit cards (check Ledger’s website for the current certification details).

Through the Ledger Live companion app, you can buy, swap, and stake thousands of coins and tokens. Your private keys never leave the device. Ledger Live runs on your connected phone or computer, but transactions are signed on the Ledger itself.

In a recent development, for those who live by the motto “don’t trust, verify,” Trezor is the gold standard. Contrary to the competitors that keep parts of their code proprietary, Trezor’s firmware is fully open-source, meaning independent security researchers constantly audit it for vulnerabilities.

The Trezor Safe 5 pairs this transparency with a vibrant color touchscreen, haptic feedback, and an EAL6+ Secure Element. It also offers a dedicated Bitcoin-only firmware option for maximalists who want to minimize attack surfaces.

When it comes to interacting with decentralized applications (DApps), decentralized exchanges (DEXs), and NFT marketplaces, MetaMask is the undisputed gateway to Web3.

Available as both a browser extension and a mobile app, MetasMask connects seamlessly to virtually every Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) network, including Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Base, and BNB Chain.

Modern updates have expanded MetaMask beyond Ethereum via MetaMask Snaps and allow people to add support for non-EVM ecosystems like Bitcoin and Solana directly inside the same interface.

Originally built as the flagship wallet for the Solana ecosystem, Phantom has evolved into one of the fastest, cleanest multi-chain wallets on the market. Today, it seamlessly supports Solana, Ethereum, Base, Polygon, and Bitcoin in a single unified interface.

In a recent development, what sets Phantom apart is user experience. Transaction simulations show you exact balance changes before you hit approve, and its automated spam filter hides malicious airdrop NFTs so beginners don’t accidentally click phishing links.

If you want one smartphone app that holds virtually every cryptocurrency in existence without manual network configuration, Trust Wallet is built for you.

Supporting over 100 blockchains and millions of digital assets, it removes the technical friction of adding custom RPC networks or hunting down token contract addresses.

It also includes a built-in Web3 browser, straightforward in-app staking for major proof-of-stake coins, and an integrated Security Scanner that flags risky smart contracts.

Many newcomers confuse the main Coinbase exchange app with Coinbase Wallet, but they are completely separate products. Coinbase Wallet is a true non-custodial wallet—meaning you hold your own 12-word recovery phrase, and Coinbase cannot freeze or access your funds.

Note that the app’s branding has changed recently: Coinbase renamed it “Base App” in July 2025 and restored the Coinbase Wallet name in September 2026. It has since shifted toward multichain trading, including perpetual futures, prediction markets, and tokenized stocks, so some of its features are now aimed at more active traders.

It has been revealed that its biggest advantage is frictionless onboarding. You can link your exchange account to transfer funds into self-custody in seconds, claim a free human-readable username instead of copying long hexadecimal addresses, and explore Base and Ethereum DApps.

Recent findings suggest that traditional hardware wallets require cables, batteries, and carefully guarding a 24-word paper backup. Tangem reimagines cold storage as a sleek, waterproof smart card—roughly the size and thickness of a standard bank debit card.

It has been revealed that to approve a transaction, you simply tap the card against the back of your NFC-enabled smartphone. Tangem comes in sets of two or three cards that act as physical backups for one another, allowing you to skip vulnerable paper seed phrases entirely (though a traditional seed option is still available if you prefer it).

Understanding the difference between hot and cold storage saves you from overpaying—or worse, leaving your funds exposed:.

A common rule of thumb among experienced crypto investors is to use both, for example keeping around 90% of long-term holdings in a cold wallet and about 10% in a hot wallet for everyday trading and Web3 exploration. This is a guideline, not a standard – adjust it to your own situation.

With crypto, there’s no bank to call if something goes wrong. Transactions are usually irreversible, and if an exchange freezes withdrawals or goes bankrupt, your funds could be stuck for months or even years.

It has been revealed that that’s why choosing the best crypto wallet matters. It gives you more control over your money and lets you manage your funds without relying on an exchange.

It has been revealed that your cryptocurrency is not stored inside the physical device—it lives on the blockchain. If your Ledger, Trezor, or Tangem card is lost, stolen, or broken, you can buy a replacement device and restore full access to your funds in minutes using your 12- or 24-word recovery phrase (or backup Tangem card).

While no system is 100% immune, cold hardware wallets cannot be hacked remotely because your private keys stay offline. Most wallet “hacks” happen when users accidentally sign a malicious smart contract on a phishing website or store their seed phrase digitally where malware can find it.

Software wallets like MetaMask, Phantom, and Trust Wallet are completely free to download and hold crypto in. Hardware wallets require an upfront purchase (typically $55 to $250). Regardless of the wallet you choose, you will still pay standard blockchain network (“gas”) fees whenever you send or swap tokens.

According to recent reports, with a custodial wallet (like a standard exchange account), a third-party company holds your private keys and can freeze or restrict your withdrawals. With a non-custodial (self-custody) wallet, only you hold the private keys—meaning nobody can block your transactions, though you are solely responsible for backing up your recovery phrase.

In a recent development, no. Unlike traditional bank accounts, funds in a self-custody crypto wallet are not covered by government deposit insurance like the FDIC or SIPC. Because you act as your own bank, protecting your recovery phrase and verifying transaction details before approving them is your primary safeguard.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that chevrolet, Cadillac, and GMC EV drivers enrolled in GM’s Energy Pass can now simply plug in to an Electrify America station to start charging. No apps or credit cards needed.

Public EV charging is getting easier and faster, with more DC fast-charging ports available and services like Plug & Charge that streamline payment.

Recent findings suggest that the technology lets you start a charging session by simply plugging in the vehicle. The session is then billed through a linked payment method, so you don’t even need to swipe a credit card or use an app.

Eligible GM electric vehicle drivers enrolled in Energy Pass can now use the service at compatible Electrify America chargers.

Industry observers note that the capability is now available for Chevrolet, Cadillac, and GMC EVs with a native CCS port (pre-2027 model year). Newer models, with a native NACS port, will gain the capability in early 2027, GM remarked.

“We’re making it easier for drivers to start a charging session and get back on the road, with an experience that has fewer steps than swiping a credit card to get gas.” Wade Sheffer, vice president of GM Energy, remarked.

Bitcoin [BTC] has slipped below the $60k mark for the second time within a week. According to CoinMarketCap data, the leading crypto was down 26.1% over the past month and 8.5% over the past week.

The rally past $80k in September fueled hopes of a bullish reversal, and it was widely accepted that the cyclical bottom might be in. Unfortunately for holders and investors, the rally didn’t last.

Relative weakness, like relative strength, is something market participants must be keenly aware of. An altcoin rallying while the rest of the market consolidates is a sign of relative strength and a good bet for continued momentum.

Equally, Bitcoin’s sell-off from the bounce to $64,603 on Monday, the 23rd of November, was worth noting.

Glassnode pointed out that stocks jumped on the news that NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Yet, within six hours of the 5% bounce, Bitcoin had retraced the move, and since then, has slipped below the $61k local support zone too.

The stock markets have also come under pressure. Nasdaq’s gains since the news came are gone. Investors are using any shred of strength to sell into, and Bitcoin was only the canary in the coal mine, wrote Glassnode.

Add to this a persistent lack of demand, and a BTC slide to $53k or even lower seems viable. In the past 20 trading days, U.S. spot BTC ETFs have shed $4.3 billion. Coinbase saw heavy selling pressure.

U.S. investors are wary of further drawdown, the data indicated.

It has been revealed that the short-term holder spent output profit ratio (STH SOPR) was at 0.99. Readings below 1.0 meant coins of this group are, on average, moving at a loss.

Sources indicate that crypto analyst Axel Adler Jr. observed that the LTH SOPR had fallen by 0.20 over the past week. It reached a 90-day low at 0.76, revealing LTH-moved coins were, on average, at deeper losses than the STH coins.

An SOPR return above 1.0 would signal the cohort’s profitability. Yet, the 22-day below-break-even LTH SOPR streak, alongside the BTC weakness and lack of demand, was a worrisome signal.

In a recent development, alphractal data showed that the onchain realized price of Bitcoin was $53,104. If these bearish conditions persist, a price drop to $53k could materialize.

OKX opened round-the-clock trading in six stock tokens at noon ET on Nov. 23, allowing eligible US customers to use the USDC stablecoin to buy and sell the tokens in the OKX app after the stock market closes.

The opening lineup pairs Coinbase (COIN), Securitize (SECZ), Strategy (MSTR), BitGo (BTGO), Robinhood (HOOD) and Circle (CRCL) with USDC.

All six recorded trades on Nov. 23 and were still the only pairs in the venue’s public asset list when checked Nov. 24. OKX indicates it has confirmed 113 assets for a rolling rollout, including stocks, ETFs and exchange-traded products.

Customers must meet geographic eligibility rules, verify their identity, activate a self-custodial CeDeFi Wallet and complete onboarding.

According to recent reports, the venue screens wallets and checks their permission before a trade. OKXICE indicates Securitize Markets tokenized the six launch stocks and that underlying shares back the tokens one-for-one through the tokenizer’s brokerage arrangements.

OKXICE LLC operates the service. The company is a joint venture between affiliates of OKX and Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the Fresh York Stock Exchange.

OKXICE indicates it operates under temporary, conditional SEC relief from the statutory definition of an exchange, and OKX says the NYSE has no role in running or overseeing the venue.

The venue indicates it stops trading a token when the exchange that lists the underlying stock halts or suspends the shares.

According to recent reports, in that case, the token can resume trading only after the primary listing exchange resumes trading in the stock. The venue’s rules also provide for stoppages tied to volume limits and risk controls.

Recent findings suggest that trades execute in Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX’s X Layer network. A buyer adds USDC to the pool and takes stock tokens out, pushing the pool price up, while a sale pushes it down.

The venue simulates the order against available liquidity before showing a quote. Liquidity providers can commit funds to specific price ranges, so order size and available funds near the current price affect what a customer gets.

USDC and stock tokens change hands through the same Uniswap v4 pool.

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Falls as PCE Inflation Comes in Hotter Than Expected.

Heavy ETF outflows, surging put bets, and fragile support leave traders watching whether a deeper slide is just beginning.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $60,000 on Wednesday, trading at around $58,220 as concerns about further losses grew ahead of Thanksgiving. The BTC price dropped 2.8% in 24 hours following the release of October inflation data, which demonstrated that price pressures remained elevated according to the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation measure.

It has been revealed that the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported that the October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose 0.3% in October, matching September’s increase.

Industry observers note that core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy, climbed 0.3% on the month and 3.3% from a year earlier. Headline PCE inflation increased 3.8% from a year earlier.

The report also indicated that US personal income rose 0.7% in October, while consumer spending increased 0.3%. However, real consumer spending was virtually unchanged, suggesting that higher prices continued to weigh on purchasing power.

Bitcoin price fell to about $55,300 over the weekend before recovering to around $64,400 on Tuesday on renewed stock market optimism after Nvidia reinstated its CEO, Jensen Huang.

However, the major crypto “acted as the canary in the coal mine”, according to Glassnode: BTC fully gave back the NVIDIA-driven rally within hours while stocks lagged, then came under pressure. Price broke the $62,000–66,000 support zone, retested summer lows, and is struggling to hold around the $60,000 level.

Bitcoin lost nearly 26% of its value over the past 30 days, and the realized losses are the heaviest since the FTX crash in November 2022.

In addition to that, approximately 90% of the tracked leveraged long positions between the previous week’s market price and Bitcoin’s realized price ($53,200) have been liquidated.

According to recent reports, glassnode suggests that much of the selling pressure is coming from the US. Over the past 20 trading days, US spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen around $4.3 billion in net outflows, marking one of their biggest periods of withdrawals since launch.

Spot market activity tells a similar story: over the past 30 days, US investors on Coinbase have been net sellers, while buying and selling on Binance have remained relatively balanced.

Industry observers note that glassnode’s latest data reveals growing bearishness among Bitcoin options traders, with limited support against sharp price movements around current levels. Between $58K and $64K, options dealers are positioned in a way that could amplify volatility, potentially accelerating a sell-off if prices fall further.

Meanwhile, bearish bets are rising. Traders bought 1.7 put options for every call last week, the highest ratio since June 2022. Similar levels of pessimism appeared near Bitcoin’s 2022 market low, although prices continued falling for several more months.

Recent findings suggest that glassnode warns that Bitcoin’s current decline may not be over. Bitcoin price remains weaker than traditional equities, US buying demand is lacking, and the market is struggling to hold its summer lows.

Glassnode identifies $60,000 as a key level to watch. A decisive break below it, followed by a close under $58,500, could open the door to a decline towards $53,200.

A recovery above $60,000, supported by renewed spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, would offer stronger evidence that the market is stabilising.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that tesla has unveiled Powercore, a solid-state medium-voltage transformer that also handles the inverter and breaker functions in a single unit.
  • It’s made in America and scheduled to start operating in 2027.
  • Update: Tesla has since released a full spec sheet for Powercore, including efficiency, warranty, and its data center aims.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that tesla has unveiled Powercore, a solid-state medium-voltage transformer that also handles the inverter and breaker functions in a single unit. Tesla rates it at 7.4 MW (9 MVA) continuously at 34.5 kV, with grid-forming support up to 10 MVA of peak power.

It’s made in America and scheduled to start operating in 2027. That’s the same year Heron Power, the startup founded by Tesla’s former top engineer Drew Baglino, looks to start volume production of its own solid-state transformer, the Heron Link.

Update: Tesla has since released a full spec sheet for Powercore, including efficiency, warranty, and its data center aims. We’ve updated the article with the fresh details.

It has been revealed that tesla first remarked it would build its own transformers in September 2025, when it unveiled Megapack 3 and Megablock. Megablock connects four Megapack 3 units to a transformer and switchgear, but Tesla shared next to nothing about the transformer itself.

Powercore is that missing piece. Tesla unveiled it today through its Tesla Megapack account on X:.

Introducing PowercoreSolid state medium voltage transformer, inverter and breaker – reliable, safe and secure7.4 MW/9 MVA continuously at 34.5 kVac w/ grid-forming support for 10MVA of peak powerMade in America. Operating 2027 pic.twitter.com/sHxqnpWJrf.

About an hour later, Tesla followed up with a much longer post on X laying out the full spec sheet:.

It has been revealed that it also packs a built-in solid-state medium-voltage breaker that Tesla says clears faults up to 1,000x faster than a conventional breaker. There’s no flammable oil, and it’s modular, so components can be serviced in the field without swapping the whole unit.

Recent findings suggest that tesla is pitching one product for three markets: battery storage, utility-scale solar, and 800 Vdc data centers. For Megablock, Powercore replaces the current two-step setup, where Megapack’s inverters output 480 V AC before a separate transformer steps it up to medium voltage. Tesla notes that old architecture had twice the losses. For solar, Powercore works as a central inverter for today’s 1,500 Vdc arrays and upcoming 2,000 Vdc systems.

Sources indicate that tesla still hasn’t shared pricing, customers, or a factory location. It only says Powercore will be made in the US “of U.S. and imported parts” with first units operating in 2027.

Sources indicate that the idea behind a solid-state transformer is simple enough. A typical solar or battery project uses low-voltage inverters to convert DC into AC, then a big oil-filled, iron-core transformer to step that up to grid voltage. A solid-state unit does both jobs with silicon carbide power electronics, which means less gear, a smaller footprint, and active control over voltage and frequency. That control is what “grid-forming” means: the unit can help hold the grid steady instead of just following it.

And with lead times on conventional transformers stretching into years as data centers and renewable projects pile into interconnection queues, there’s real demand for an alternative.

You can’t look at Powercore without thinking of Heron Power.

In a recent development, baglino spent 18 years at Tesla and finished as SVP of powertrain and energy, in charge of batteries, motors, power electronics, and energy products. He left in April 2024 and introduced Heron Power in 2025 to build solid-state transformers.

He brought a lot of Tesla’s power electronics talent with him. As we reported when Tesla first revealed its transformer plans, Heron hired engineers who led power electronics design for Powerwall 3, the next-gen Megapack, and Superchargers, along with the person who ran Tesla’s power electronics controls team for charging and energy products.

Sources indicate that since then, Heron has raised a $38 million Series A, a $140 million Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz and Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and a $60 million credit facility from J.P. Morgan and TriplePoint Capital. Former Tesla CFO Zach Kirkhorn sits on its board, and Tesla co-founder JB Straubel is an investor.

It’s also building Heron Factory One, a 286,000-square-foot plant in Morgan Hill, California, designed to make 10,000 Heron Links a year. That’s over 40 GW of annual capacity, with commercial production planned for late 2027.

And the customers are lining up. Vantage reserved more than 1 GW for its data centers, Intersect reserved 1.5 GW, LG Energy Solution Vertech is integrating Heron Link with its US-made battery systems, and RWE signed a pilot to install Heron Links at a Texas battery storage site in April 2027. Baglino says Heron has 50 GW of orders in the pipeline.

Here’s how the two compare based on what each organization has disclosed:.

On paper, Powercore is the bigger box, and now it has the better numbers too. At 7.4 MW continuous, it carries about 50% more power per unit than the 5 MW Heron Link, and its 98.86% peak efficiency edges out Heron’s 98.6%. But Tesla’s figure is a peak number, and Heron doesn’t label its own as one, so it’s not quite apples to apples. Neither company has shared pricing.

Industry observers note that tesla is also going straight at Heron’s data center pitch. Powercore converts medium voltage directly to 800 Vdc, the rack architecture Nvidia is pushing, and Tesla indicates it’s working with Nvidia on 800 Vdc designs. Heron’s data center version does the same 34.5 kV AC to 800 VDC conversion with built-in storage, and data centers make up about a third of its business. Tesla’s answer to the storage piece is Megapack on the DC bus, and it says it already has 10 GWh of Megapack running at data centers.

This one is a little awkward for Tesla.

A big chunk of the people who designed Tesla’s power electronics over the last decade now work at Heron, and the guy who ran the whole org is its CEO. Tesla’s energy business also lost its longtime leader, Mike Snyder, last month, according to the WSJ.

This is all wrong. Tesla started developing this 3 years ago. Before Heron. The team selling Powercore is same as Megapack that has a way larger customer base than Heron. Also Heron is not a bankable company per project finance terms. So they will struggle to get projects financed through equity and senior debt . Not as Tesla.

In a recent development, to be fair, Tesla still has plenty of power electronics expertise. Its silicon carbide inverters are in millions of cars and every Megapack. And it has something Heron doesn’t: a massive installed base and a sales channel. Tesla states it’s almost sold out of Megapacks for 2027, and bundling Powercore into Megablock is an easy upsell. Plenty of developers will take the one-stop shop.

Sources indicate that tesla’s specs now match or beat Heron’s on paper. But Heron has named customers, a pilot site with an install date, and a factory under construction. Tesla has none of those yet. I wouldn’t be surprised if Heron is actually ahead here.

But either way, the transformer shortage is big enough for both companies to sell everything they can build.

As data centers and upcoming solar and battery projects pile onto the grid, utilities are scrambling for equipment and passing those costs on to ratepayers.
