📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that investors supplied about $6 million in tokenized high-yield bond fund shares as collateral on Aave Horizon’s lending market by Nov. 24.

Eligible holders can pledge the shares (HINC) to borrow stablecoins while keeping their investment in the fund, but only fund-approved recipients can take those shares in a liquidation.

Recent findings suggest that aavescan’s snapshots showed deposits rising from 0.152 HINC on Nov. 23 to about 6,200 HINC on Nov. 24. The reserve displayed roughly $6 million in deposits at 18:14 UTC on Nov. 24.

Horizon’s public market data reports stablecoin loans across the market, but leaves open whether any of those loans are backed by HINC.

According to recent reports, HINC represents shares in the Neuberger Securitize High Income Tokenized Fund, advised by Securitize Capital and sub-advised by Neuberger Berman Investment Advisers. The strategy focuses on high-yield corporate bonds and can also invest in slices of collateralized loan obligations, bank loans, and other fixed income.

According to recent reports, holders can pledge HINC without redeeming their shares. The listing proposal states the fund restricts the tokens to approved wallets that have passed identity and compliance checks.

Sources indicate that in a Nov. 24 post, Aave stated eligible holders could borrow USDC, GHO, or RLUSD.

Recent findings suggest that aave’s live reserve overview showed a 55% maximum initial loan-to-value ratio and a 67% liquidation threshold for standard HINC positions. Both percentages compare debt with the value of the pledged shares.

Recent findings suggest that A drop in the fund’s value can move an existing loan closer to liquidation even if the borrower draws no additional stablecoins. In the GHO-only setting, called E-Mode, the limit was 57%, and the threshold was 69%.

Both settings revealed an 8% liquidation penalty, and the same reserve overview listed a 10,000 HINC cap on total deposits.

Under Securitize’s liquidation design, a preapproved liquidator repays debt in the borrowed stablecoin and receives the underlying HINC in an eligible wallet.

It has been revealed that securitize’s transfer agent then records the liquidator as the upcoming holder. The token enforces those transfer restrictions when the collateral changes hands.

A fund-approved wallet is required to take HINC from a liquidated position.

The liquidator commits stablecoins upfront and waits for the fund to pay out.

The sequence describes an approved liquidator using ordinary fund redemption. The payout target is not guaranteed. The public evidence does not establish financing capacity under stress.

It has been revealed that maps the liquidation steps described in the Aave governance review and the redemption settlement target on Securitize’s fund page. Connector spacing is illustrative.

The sequence describes an approved liquidator using ordinary fund redemption. The payout target is not guaranteed. The public evidence does not establish financing capacity under stress.

The fund targets next-business-day redemption payouts, and says settlement can take longer depending on the liquidity of its investments.

Sources indicate that securitize claims the shares have no secondary market. A liquidator who redeems through the fund pays the stablecoin debt upfront and carries the shares until the payout arrives.

If several positions need liquidating while redemptions are pending, approved buyers would need enough stablecoins to fund those repayments. The amount of collateral approved liquidators can absorb under stress remains untested in the public reserve data.

Zcash holders just got a new update as the major crypto exchange Gemini has announced support for Shielded Zcash deposits.

It has been revealed that scott Merkel, 'Wolf of All Streets,' shared this update in an X post, highlighting the milestone as the first of its kind for any major exchange. According to Merkel, Gemini now lets customers deposit Zcash (ZEC) to shielded addresses, saying it is the first major exchange with both shielded deposits and withdrawals.

GEMINI NOW LETS CUSTOMERS DEPOSIT ZCASH $ZEC TO SHIELDED ADDRESSES, SAYING IT IS THE FIRST MAJOR EXCHANGE WITH BOTH SHIELDED DEPOSITS AND WITHDRAWALS https://t.co/d9pIFJ6uJM.

Gemini co-founder Tyler Winklevoss shared the milestone in a recent X post, adding that the recent move builds on the launch of shielded Zcash withdrawals on Gemini this summer.

In July 2026, shortly after the Ironwood upgrade was activated, Gemini rolled out support for shielded Zcash withdrawals to the newly introduced Ironwood pool, allowing customers to send Zcash from Gemini to their Ironwood deposit address. Ironwood (NU6.3) went live on July 28, 2026, at block height 3,428,143, bringing a new shielded pool for Zcash.

With the recent launch of support for Shielded Zcash deposits, Gemini people can make Shielded Zcash deposits and withdrawals to and from Ironwood, with Winklevoss remarking that the private movement of money was now complete.

Zcash's total shielded supply now sits at around 4.93 million ZEC (around 28.94% of total ZEC supply) as of November 25, 2026.

November has brought in key updates for the Zcash network. Zcash's NU7 upgrade went live earlier in November 2026, slashing ZEC's target block time to 25 seconds from 75 seconds. The upcoming 25-second block target lets miners add a batch of transactions to the chain three times as often.

In a recent development, none of this prints extra ZEC. Each block pays a third as much and halvings come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving.

According to recent reports, days after the NU7 upgrade, the Zcash Foundation followed up with the release of Zebra 7.1.0, which fixed ten security advisories, most of which closed off ways in which another node on the network (a peer) could stop a Zebra node from catching up with the chain or make it run out of memory. It also added sync and memory diagnostics, automatic peer recovery, and clearer errors.

BMW’s first US-built EV promises 456 miles of range and ultra-fast charging

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.
  • BMW officially opened its fresh Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.
  • The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-fresh iX5 SUV.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iX5 is BMW’s first fully electric vehicle built in the US, promising an estimated up to 456 miles of range, ultra-fast charging speeds, and plenty of Neue Klasse tech.

BMW officially opened its fresh Plant Woodruff in South Carolina on November 13, marking the start of series production of its sixth-generation (Gen6) electric vehicle batteries.

The Gen6 batteries will power BMW’s upcoming “X” electric vehicles, starting with the all-fresh iX5 SUV.

The iX5 is being built about 15 miles away at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg, the company’s first fully electric model to be assembled in the US.

BMW Plant Spartanburg is churning out around 70 iX5s a day following a $1.7 billion investment in South Carolina to expand the plant for EV production and build the upcoming battery assembly plant in Woodruff.

According to Robert Engelhorn, president and CEO of BMW Manufacturing in Spartanburg, the company is confident the iX5 will attract buyers, promising 435 miles of range, ultra-fast charging, and its updated Neue Klasse technology and design.

Engelhorn told Automotive News in an interview that “there’s a clear trend globally for EVs,” adding that “We will contribute to this growth from the BMW side.”.

BMW didn’t provide a specific production estimate for the iX5, but suppliers were reportedly told it would be around 60,000 EVs in 2027, down from 100,000 it initially forecasted.

“We said we would begin assembling fully electric BMW vehicles in the US by the end of 2026 – and we are delivering on that commitment,” Engelhorn said.

A company spokesperson confirmed that the iX5 will initially use battery cells from China before switching to US-sourced cells from LG Energy Solutions plant in Arizona by the end of the decade.

With production now underway, the iX5 is expected to begin arriving at US dealerships in early 2027.

The 2027 BMW iX5 60 xDrive starts at $79,800. BMW estimates the 144 kWh battery will provide up to 456 miles of range, up from the 435 miles it previously estimated.

It has been revealed that it features BMW’s new “double-X” light signature, which combines the headlights, daytime running lights, side lights, and turn signals into one unit. The Double-X headlights come standard, but BMW said you can switch them for simpler diagonal stripes.

Last month, BMW showcased the i5’s ultra-fast-charging capabilities during a media event in Southern California with IONNA and Alpitronic.

During the demo, the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW, which BMW noted enables it to add an impressive up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that the electric SUV features a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain setup that delivers a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque. BMW notes it can go from 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds and tow up to 6,000 lbs.

Inside, the iX5 adopts BMW’s Neue Klasse design and tech, like the smaller iX3 SUV. The setup includes a new 17.9″ infotainment touchscreen and BMW’s Panoramic Vision, which spans the bottom of the windshield. There’s also an optional 14.6″ passenger screen for a third display.

This is at the top of our short list. Out of Spec got 411 miles at 70 mph (by contrast the Gravity rated at 450 got 368 on the same run and the R1S rated at 410 got 349). It is a real 400+ mile vehicle with an ability to charge a real 300 miles in ~20 minutes.

Edit: OOS was with 22" wheels rated at 426. It should get >430 with the standard 21" wheels.

Measuring 197.2″ long, 78.7″ wide, and 68.9″ tall, BMW’s new iX5 is about the size of the Porsche Cayenne Electric.

Industry observers note that by 2030, BMW aims to be assembling at least fully electric models at Plant Spartanburg. “This marks the beginning of the next chapter in the success story of the largest plant in our global production network,” Raymond Wittman, BMW’s head of production, stated.

Following Debrecen (Hungary), Irlbach-Straßkirchen (Germany), and Shenyang (China), Woodruff is the fourth site in BMW’s production network to begin series production of the Gen6 batteries.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home » Trendsetter News » NYSE’s Avalanche Pick Hints At XRP’s Role.
  • NYSE’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily rule out XRP.
  • The Upcoming York Stock Exchange’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily shut out XRP, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her latest video.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » NYSE’s Avalanche Pick Hints At XRP’s Role.

NYSE’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily rule out XRP.

The Upcoming York Stock Exchange’s reported choice of Avalanche for a tokenized-stock platform does not necessarily shut out XRP, wealth commentator Kamilah Stevenson argues in her latest video.

Her distinction: settling share ownership and moving money across currencies are separate jobs, and winning one does not automatically secure the other.

In a recent development, according to Dr. Stevenson, Ava Labs confirmed that Avalanche would provide the core ledger for the clearing firm behind the proposed platform.

She cites Wall Street Journal reporting that Avalanche would be its sole settlement blockchain, with regulatory approval still required.

It has been revealed that the proposed venue would support around-the-clock trading and near-instant settlement. Stevenson says NYSE tested Avalanche for roughly a year, prioritizing transaction speed, predictable costs and control over who can participate.

That permissioning capability matters for a regulated exchange. Avalanche (AVAX) can support customized networks with participation restrictions, rather than requiring the exchange to conduct settlement on an unrestricted public network.

Industry observers note that AVAX rose as much as roughly 10% on the news, according to the video. Stevenson, who discloses holding the token, calls the selection a win for Avalanche, but cautions against treating infrastructure adoption as proof of investment returns.

“A network being used by a massive name and its token being needed” are different things, she says. The announcement, in her account, provided neither revenue figures nor a commitment that NYSE would buy or hold AVAX.

Sources indicate that dr. Stevenson’s XRP thesis centers on overseas investors funding dollar-denominated stock purchases outside conventional banking hours.

A trader holding yen or another currency would need access to dollars or dollar-linked funding before buying U.S. shares.

In a recent development, she argues that this creates an opportunity for cross-border payment infrastructure, including XRP. But it remains a proposed use case, not a disclosed partnership: “I’m not telling you that NYSE is going to pick XRP for that.”.

Recent findings suggest that the YouTube video episode does not establish that XRP would be necessary for such funding. Nor does expanded trading access, by itself, demonstrate future demand for the token.

It has been revealed that dr. Kamilah Stevenson also notes the platform would support tokenized stocks issued across multiple blockchains, distinguishing asset issuance from the ledger used for settlement.

Those details matter more than a simple Avalanche-versus-XRP contest: the unresolved questions are which services institutions actually adopt, what generates revenue, and whether that activity requires either token.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • More investment managers reported holding US spot Bitcoin products in the third quarter, but the growth in their positions came from a much smaller group.
  • Sources indicate that galaxy Research found that the 25 largest holders at Sept.
  • 19 analysis of Form 13F filings counted 2,166 investment managers with positions as of Sept.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More investment managers reported holding US spot Bitcoin products in the third quarter, but the growth in their positions came from a much smaller group.

Sources indicate that galaxy Research found that the 25 largest holders at Sept. 30 added more Bitcoin exposure than all reporting managers combined. Everyone outside that group, taken together, cut exposure.

Sources indicate that galaxy's Nov. 19 analysis of Form 13F filings counted 2,166 investment managers with positions as of Sept. 30, up 191 from June. Their disclosed holdings reached nearly $29.8 billion, or the equivalent of 356,491 BTC, across 13 US spot products, including an over-the-counter trust.

The Bitcoin-equivalent figure translates fund shares into their underlying Bitcoin exposure.

The filings describe a quarter that ended weeks before US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly $2.4 billion in net outflows over five trading sessions through Nov. 23.

The 25 largest managers at the end of September held 60.8% of the disclosed exposure in Galaxy's dataset, and added a net 56,922 BTC-equivalent over the quarter.

The rest of the reporting managers reduced their holdings by 7,693 BTC-equivalent combined, leaving an overall net addition of 49,229.

Recent findings suggest that galaxy ranks the group by holdings on Sept. 30 and converts the change in reported shares into BTC-equivalent at September-end rates. A rising Bitcoin price alone cannot account for the increase.

The 25 largest filers added more than the total net increase, while other managers trimmed their exposure.

The top 25 held 60.8% of disclosed exposure and accounted for the whole net increase.

Form 13F captures reportable long share positions. The comparison covers disclosed holdings in Galaxy’s 13-product sample, including one OTC trust, and cannot identify underlying clients or offsetting positions.

Recent findings suggest that galaxy ranked filers by Sept. 30, 2026 positions across 13 U.S. spot Bitcoin products. The top 25 held 60.8%. The remainder is 100% minus 60.8%, or 39.2%. The change for other filers is 49,229 minus 56,922, or −7,693 BTC-equivalent. Change bars use the same zero and unit.

According to recent reports, form 13F captures reportable long share positions. The comparison covers disclosed holdings in Galaxy’s 13-product sample, including one OTC trust, and cannot identify underlying clients or offsetting positions.

Widening the group to the 50 largest holders makes the offset clearer. They added 59,578 BTC-equivalent, while everyone else cut 10,349.

Wells Fargo led the additions at 14,636 BTC-equivalent, followed by Brevan Howard at 8,606, Bank of America at 7,201, Millennium Management at 7,114, and Jane Street at 6,180.

Wells Fargo finished September with 30,553 BTC-equivalent in reported exposure, moving ahead of Jane Street, which ended the quarter at 23,167.

Sources indicate that galaxy counted 358 managers that disclosed positions after reporting none in June, while 167 dropped out. The newcomers had a combined 9,554 BTC-equivalent, just 2.7% of the reported holdings at quarter-end.

In a recent development, separately, Bloomberg senior ETF analyst James Seyffart reported on Nov. 24 that more than 2,200 institutions held Bitcoin ETFs and stated investment advisers dominated known ownership in his analysis.

A manager with a small newly disclosed position counts just as much toward participation as a large platform taking a much bigger position. And an existing holder can add a position worth far more than those newcomers put together without changing the headcount.

More managers can bring a wider set of investors into the funds while leaving the net increase sensitive to changes in a few large positions.

Across the 12 exchange-listed products Galaxy tracked, 13F filers accounted for 27.6% of the Bitcoin in the funds at Sept. 30.

According to recent reports, the 10 largest filers held 41.9% of that disclosed exposure. A handful of financial groups can dominate the positions visible in those filings, while most of the funds’ Bitcoin backs shares held outside the 13F tally.

Galaxy’s breakdown traced 26,016 BTC-equivalent to Wells Fargo’s adviser and brokerage arms at the end of September, up from 13,219 in June.

The increase at Bank of America came mainly from its dealer and trading units, whose reported positions reached 7,626 BTC-equivalent, up from 421 in June.

Brokerage positions can include assets managed for clients, while trading positions can include inventory or one side of a hedge. SEC guidance on Form 13F requires managers to report eligible positions over which they exercise investment discretion and to leave short positions out.

A filing can show a sizable long position even if a trade elsewhere offsets some of its sensitivity to Bitcoin's price. It also gives little visibility into how many underlying investors sit behind a brokerage unit's reported position.

Across the 12 listed products, Galaxy put advisers and wealth platforms at 40.5% of reported September holdings. That category includes broker-dealer platforms, whose dealer and trading desks can also contribute to the totals.

The category added about half of the net increase in that product set.

According to recent reports, the September quarter ended with Bitcoin at $83,580, according to Galaxy. By Nov. 16 it was $64,943, and the funds Galaxy tracked held 38,531 fewer BTC than at quarter-end.

The daily US spot Bitcoin ETF figures from Farside Investors then indicated five consecutive sessions of net withdrawals from Nov. 17 through Nov. 23. Withdrawals reached $669.2 million on Nov. 20 and $569.7 million on Nov. 23.

Recent findings suggest that daily net flows in USD millions. Dates show November 2026 trading sessions.

It has been revealed that source: Farside Investors, daily U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF flows.

An ETF can see withdrawals while some holders retain or add to their positions, as the largest holders increased their exposure in the third quarter while other filers cut theirs overall.

The next set of filings can show which September positions were still reported at December’s quarter-end and whether managers outside September’s top 25 increased their combined exposure.

The headcount measures participation among filers, while the distribution of changes demonstrates whether the increase in reported fund-share exposure is spreading across more of those managers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that bitcoin [BTC] ETFs faced their worst month since launch, recording approximately $4.94 billion in Net Outflows during November so far.
  • Yet institutional ownership data offered a different perspective.
  • According to recent reports, just for a quick recap, the year started weak.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that bitcoin [BTC] ETFs faced their worst month since launch, recording approximately $4.94 billion in Net Outflows during November so far. With several days still left, the month had already overtaken June’s $4.51 billion withdrawal.

Yet institutional ownership data offered a different perspective. Billions were leaving the funds, while reported institutional exposure remained substantial.

According to recent reports, just for a quick recap, the year started weak. January recorded $1.61 billion in Net Outflows, followed by $206.52 million in February.

Recent findings suggest that A brief recovery followed. March attracted $1.32 billion in Net Inflows, while April brought another $1.97 billion. May, however, recorded $2.43 billion in Net Outflows. June followed with $4.51 billion, making it the year’s second-worst month.

According to recent reports, july’s $172.43 million in Net Inflows offered a near-flat pause before a stronger rebound. August attracted $3.52 billion, followed by $2.65 billion in September. That recovery unravelled in October, when $515.03 million left the funds. November’s $4.94 billion withdrawal then pushed the year towards another low.

In fact, Glassnode also pointed out that Bitcoin ETF trading volume has fallen below its median since launch.

Hence, the persistent selling pressure has raised concerns about institutional confidence in Bitcoin. This is because a closer look at institutional ownership data suggests that Wall Street is not abandoning Bitcoin ETFs just yet.

In fact, institutional participation has continued to expand despite the deteriorating market sentiment, raising an key question: What is keeping institutions invested in Bitcoin ETFs when investors are pulling billions out of them?

According to Bloomberg ETF analyst James Seyffart, 2,223 institutional filers collectively reported approximately $29.77 billion in Bitcoin ETF exposure, equivalent to 356,072 BTC.

It has been revealed that investment advisors accounted for the largest share, with 1,863 filers holding approximately 160,195 BTC worth $13.39 billion. Brokerage firms followed with 59,255 BTC, while hedge funds held approximately 58,088 BTC. Banks and trusts also have considerable exposure, holding 28,937 BTC and 19,723 BTC, respectively.

Industry observers note that more importantly, the data shows that institutional ownership increased by 56,493 BTC over the one-year period. Well, according to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions have also added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period.

Industry observers note that this suggests that the recent outflow streak has not translated into a complete institutional retreat. In this, Wells Fargo has emerged as a major institutional holder, with its aggregated filings showing approximately 30,549 BTC in exposure.

According to recent reports, jane Street, Goldman Sachs, Millennium Management, and Morgan Stanley were also featured among the notable holders. However, the current selling pressure cannot be overlooked.

Ecoinometrics noted that November’s ETF flow trajectory was closely following its bearish simulation. Therefore, if the trend continues, its model suggests Bitcoin could potentially revisit the low-$50,000 range.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Latest data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant highlights that about 4.61 billion XRP have flowed into crypto exchanges over the last 30 days.
  • According to the data, Binance has led all other crypto exchanges in the amount of XRP inflows received over the last month as its users appear to have panicked amid rising market struggles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

XRP has continued to see traders deposit large amounts of tokens into exchanges, including Binance, Bybit and others, as the prolonged market volatility has triggered increased fear across the broader crypto market.

Latest data from the crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant highlights that about 4.61 billion XRP have flowed into crypto exchanges over the last 30 days.

According to the data, Binance has led all other crypto exchanges in the amount of XRP inflows received over the last month as its users appear to have panicked amid rising market struggles.

As such, Binance recorded about 1.221 billion XRP deposits during the period, representing the lion's share of the total inflows.

Ranking second on the list is OKX, which followed with about 866.51 million XRP, while Bybit was next with 662.57 million XRP.

The trend extended to other exchanges, even though they saw considerably lower inflows: Upbit saw about 176.96 million XRP flow into its exchange during the same period, while Bitget recorded inflows of about 140.02 million XRP.

Although the past month has seen billions of XRP transferred back to exchanges, further data shows that the 4.6 billion XRP inflow is substantially lower when compared with inflows seen in October.

In October, the total XRP that flowed into exchanges throughout the month was estimated at around 6 billion XRP, suggesting that XRP selling pressure has eased compared with the previous month.

This has drawn attention across the crypto market as the price of XRP suffered larger losses this month compared with last month, sparking questions about whether investor confidence is recovering.

Institutional progress continues, but the development of Ripple’s custody service doesn’t spark up a rally.

According to recent reports, XRP’s price briefly climbed above $1 this week, reaching roughly $1.03 before sellers pushed it back below the level within hours. The move followed a rebound from near $0.91, leaving the token trading around $0.93 to $0.96.

Industry observers note that the push above $1 was helped in part by traders closing bearish futures positions. XRP short liquidations made up a substantial share of recent XRP futures liquidations, a dynamic that can produce sharp rallies without durable buying.

Spot-market data has shown sellers retaining the upper hand in recent weeks, though the pace of net selling has eased. Large crypto holders accumulated an estimated $72 million in XRP over several days, standing apart from reported selling in Bitcoin and Ether (ETH).

In a recent development, that activity has not yet turned $1 from resistance into a reliable floor. XRP was rejected around the level more than once during the latest stretch of trading.

According to recent reports, the price weakness has continued even as Ripple expands its institutional footprint. Yapı Kredi, one of Türkiye’s largest private banks, looks to use Ripple Custody for digital-asset services connected to its crypto platform, with the infrastructure operated on the bank’s own premises.

In a recent development, ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin has also grown. Its circulating supply recently reached a high near $2.87 billion, briefly overtaking USD1 before subsequent redemptions put the rival token marginally back ahead.

Sources indicate that 💵 Ripple's RLUSD has overtaken Trump-linked USD1 by circulating supply, hitting a record $2.87B. Ripple's stablecoin keeps growing, even in a bear market. The onchain dollar keeps growing. This is where real adoption is happening.#RLUSD #Ripple #Stablecoins.

About $761 million of RLUSD supply is held on the XRP Ledger, where XRP is used to pay transaction fees.

Those developments strengthen Ripple’s broader payments, custody and stablecoin business, but they do not automatically create immediate buying pressure for XRP.

Turkish XRP trading against the lira, for example, has fallen sharply from year-earlier levels despite the bank custody announcement.

XRP’s price has lost about 26% over the past month and remains well below its longer-term trend averages. The altcoin now trades just one cent above the low-tier Bollinger Band (BOLL).

A break above the recent high near $1.03 could bring the $1.04 to $1.08 area into view, while failure to hold the $0.91 to $0.92 support zone could expose $0.86.

Ripple’s institutional progress may matter over a longer horizon, but XRP investors are still waiting for that momentum to show up decisively in the market.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • VanEck is ending its relationship with Gemini across three spot crypto ETFs, leaving Coinbase Custody as its remaining named custodian.
  • In a recent development, the asset manager disclosed in Nov.
  • According to recent reports, the agreements are scheduled to expire in February 2027, and Gemini will continue to provide services until the termination takes effect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VanEck is ending its relationship with Gemini across three spot crypto ETFs, leaving Coinbase Custody as its remaining named custodian.

In a recent development, the asset manager disclosed in Nov. 19 regulatory filings that it had notified Gemini of plans to terminate its custody and clearing agreements for its Bitcoin ETF (HODL), Ethereum ETF (ETHV) and Solana ETF (VSOL).

According to recent reports, the agreements are scheduled to expire in February 2027, and Gemini will continue to provide services until the termination takes effect. The decision also ends a separate arrangement under which Gemini facilitates Solana staking for VSOL.

The filings did not disclose the reasons for the termination or how much cryptocurrency VanEck at the moment holds with Gemini.

The three funds have attracted approximately $1.15 billion in cumulative net inflows since their respective debuts and collectively managed $934.2 million in net assets as of Nov. 24, according to SoSoValue data.

VanEck's Bitcoin ETF accounted for the bulk of that exposure, with $977.1 million in cumulative net inflows and $848.2 million in net assets. Its Ethereum and Solana funds recorded cumulative net inflows of $151.6 million and $19.2 million, respectively.

According to recent reports, vanEck's decision extends beyond asset safekeeping. Gemini also provides clearing infrastructure that helps the funds settle cryptocurrency transactions associated with ETF share creations and redemptions.

Under the existing arrangements, VanEck's funds can use Gemini Clearing to complete trades negotiated with liquidity providers that are also Gemini customers.

The service has supported cash-based orders, which require the funds to purchase or sell cryptocurrencies, and in-kind transactions involving the direct transfer of digital assets.

The scheduled February 2027 exit affects two services across VanEck’s HODL, ETHV and VSOL.

According to recent reports, coinbase Custody stays with all three funds. The filings name no successor to Gemini’s trade clearing service.

In a recent development, the lines track service appointments. The filings give no amount or timing for any transfers between custodians.

The connections trace each service described in the three November 19 termination filings across its scheduled effective date.

In a recent development, the lines track service appointments. The filings give no amount or timing for any transfers between custodians.

Coinbase will continue serving the Bitcoin and Ethereum funds under their existing prime broker agreements, while the Solana fund also maintains a separate custody agreement with the firm.

VanEck did not identify a successor to Gemini's clearing services or provide a timetable for any cryptocurrency transfers between the custodians.

VanEck's decision contrasts with arrangements at other major US crypto ETF issuers that have established relationships with multiple digital asset custodians.

According to recent reports, blackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) uses Coinbase Custody as its custodian and has appointed Anchorage Digital Bank as an additional provider. Its latest quarterly report noted the fund had no immediate plans to transfer Bitcoin to Anchorage.

Recent findings suggest that blackRock also maintains flexibility in its trading arrangements. The fund can execute Bitcoin transactions directly with third-party counterparties or through Coinbase Prime when processing cash-based creation and redemption orders.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund maintains its primary custody and trade execution relationship with Fidelity Digital Assets, an affiliate of its sponsor. Fidelity has also appointed BitGo Bank & Trust as an additional custodian, although it reported no immediate plans to transfer Bitcoin to the company.

These arrangements allow BlackRock and Fidelity to retain additional custody providers without necessarily distributing their existing Bitcoin holdings across them.

VanEck's termination of Gemini's agreements moves in the opposite direction across three separate crypto investment products, increasing the importance of its remaining relationship with Coinbase.

Its September quarterly reports describe transactions conducted directly with liquidity providers, while earlier prospectuses also allowed alternative execution arrangements for certain trades if settlement failed.

Those existing arrangements could accommodate transactions previously handled through Gemini Clearing without VanEck appointing another dedicated clearing provider.

With the termination scheduled for February, VanEck's subsequent regulatory disclosures could reveal whether it intends to consolidate more of its trading infrastructure with Coinbase or establish latest arrangements with other institutional service providers.

Morgan Stanley has disclosed its latest crypto-related holdings in a quarterly Form 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. According to the filing, the bank's U.S. equity portfolio was valued at around $1.96 trillion as of Sept. 30, up from $1.89 trillion at the end of June.

Most of the crypto-related positions in the filing are Bitcoin products and Bitcoin-linked stocks, and the bank also reported a small amount of XRP exposure through three spot exchange-traded funds.

The largest crypto-related position in the filing is Strategy (MSTR). Morgan Stanley held around 10.88 million MSTR shares worth about $1.67 billion at the end of September, up from 9.33 million shares at the end of the second quarter.

The bank also increased its position in BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) from 16.48 million to 19.52 million shares, and the IBIT stake was worth about $924 million as of Sept. 30.

Besides, Morgan Stanley reported 6.72 million units of its own Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust (MSBT), up from 2.57 million units at the end of June. In the second-quarter filing, the MSBT position was worth about $43.3 million. MSBT started trading on NYSE Arca in April, and it was the first spot Bitcoin ETF issued by a major U.S. bank.

Among crypto stocks, Morgan Stanley also held around 10.54 million Robinhood (HOOD) shares worth about $1.19 billion and 3.72 million Coinbase (COIN) shares worth about $694 million.

Morgan Stanley reported $116,097 in XRP ETF holdings as of Sept. 30. Franklin's XRP fund accounted for $111,885 of that amount, REX-Osprey's fund for $3,098, and the Bitwise XRP ETF for the remaining $1,114.

In a recent development, the bank held the same three funds at the end of June. In the second quarter, Morgan Stanley reported 6,715 shares of the Franklin fund, 255 shares of the REX-Osprey fund and 67 shares of the Bitwise fund. Before that, the bank's first-quarter filing showed 1,700 shares of the Volatility Shares XRP ETF and 100 shares of the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF worth $15,488 in total.

On Wednesday, XRP was trading at around $0.908, down 2.23% over 24 hours, according to CoinMarketCap.

Morgan Stanley was one of seven banks that disclosed XRP-linked ETF holdings in third-quarter 13F filings. The positions of the seven banks totaled about $29.4 million as of Sept. 30, and Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo accounted for $27.21 million of that amount.

Goldman Sachs reported much larger XRP positions. The bank's XRP ETF holdings rose from $87 million in the second quarter to $144 million in the third quarter, and Goldman's crypto portfolio was worth around $2.64 billion in total.

Morning Minute: Jensen Returns, Markets Soar (Except Crypto)

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner.
  • Six days after Nvidia’s board chair told investors “the Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” the board voted unanimously to reinstate him as president, CEO and director, effective immediately.
  • Nvidia shares rose 33% to around $167, adding roughly a trillion dollars of market value in a session.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Six days after Nvidia’s board chair told investors “the Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” the board voted unanimously to reinstate him as president, CEO and director, effective immediately.

Nvidia shares rose 33% to around $167, adding roughly a trillion dollars of market value in a session. Huang’s personal net worth climbed about $36.6 billion on his 3.5% stake, moving him to 13th on the Forbes global list. Short sellers took roughly $12.2 billion in paper losses, their worst single day since at least 2019, which wiped out the $10.5 billion they had booked the prior week.

It has been revealed that the stock market absolutely ripped on the news. The Nasdaq closed up 6.51% at 24,089, its best day since April 2025. The S&P gained 4.7%, the Dow was +3%, and the VIX collapsed 25.8% to 26.62.

Bitcoin went along with the ride—for a few hours. It touched $63,929 intraday, up 5.1%, then spent the afternoon handing it back and finished near $61,000, barely up on the day. The ETFs used the pump to exit more, with BTC ETFs seeing another $570M in outflows on the day.

Sources indicate that ETH and other majors also closed red. Alts gave back their gains. And the CMC top 20 index managed just 0.20% gain.

In a recent development, that’s a 19 to 1 ratio between what the Nasdaq captured and what Bitcoin kept, on the same catalyst, on the same day. Pain for the crypto bulls.

Industry observers note that what makes it even more painful, is that crypto fell with AI stocks the whole way down, and the standard explanation was that both trade on the same liquidity and the same risk appetite. Monday tested that and the correlation fell through. The AI trade got a catalyst and markets bounced. Crypto didn’t bounce with it.

Sources indicate that as for Nvidia’s reversal decision itself, questions remain to say the least. The board claims it was satisfied with Huang’s “candor and ability to lead,” and that input from senior U.S. officials left it confident his return “poses no national security risk.” Trump publicly pushed for it and stated the board had sought assurance on the espionage allegations. What actually changed between November 17 and November 23 hasn’t been explained. The independent directors’ investigation is still open, and Nvidia is now standing up a board committee for national security and export-control oversight plus recruiting a chief compliance officer.

Perhaps answers will trickle out over time. The AI trade may not need them anyway. And crypto, well, it's in its own world right now, waiting for its own catalysts (likely quantum-related). But it’s very unclear that catalyst is coming in 2026, and it’s becoming clear that many are not interested in waiting for the answers….

Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., is moving into asset management with a new subsidiary that will offer custody clients a way to earn yield on their bitcoin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., is moving into asset management with a new subsidiary that will offer custody clients a way to earn yield on their bitcoin.

The unit, called 61st Parallel Asset Management, is expected to start operating by early December, CEO Nathan McCauley remarked in an interview to CoinDesk. Its first product will be a bitcoin-denominated fund, meaning returns are measured in BTC rather than dollars. The name nods to the city of Anchorage, Alaska, which sits at 61 degrees north latitude.

“We have increasingly heard clients say they want to earn on top of the assets they hold at Anchorage — something that’s very common among the large financial institutions of the world,” McCauley said.

Sources indicate that anchorage has filed a Form ADV, the disclosure document investment advisers use to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission or state regulators, or to report as exempt advisers. The form covers a firm’s ownership, business, assets under management, fees and conflicts of interest. As of Tuesday afternoon, the SEC’s public adviser database revealed no record for 61st Parallel, so the filing’s details were not yet public.

According to recent reports, the entity itself is not fresh. New York state records show that 61st Parallel Asset Management LLC, a Delaware tech giant, registered to do business in New York on July 8, listing an office on Park Avenue South in Manhattan.

Industry observers note that anchorage already lets clients earn on some holdings. Its website lists staking, which pays rewards for helping secure proof-of-stake networks, and a separate rewards product for eligible assets. Bitcoin runs on proof-of-work and cannot be staked natively.

Anchorage has not remarked publicly how the fund will generate yield, what it will charge or which clients will qualify. Those details matter to bitcoin holders, because bitcoin pays no interest on its own. Common ways to earn on it include lending coins out, posting them as collateral or selling options against them, and each carries its own risk.

Recent findings suggest that public companies have already tested some of those approaches. Trump Media disclosed this month that it had pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can rehypothecate, or reuse, the coins.

It has been revealed that founded in 2017, Anchorage received a national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in January 2021, the first crypto firm to win one. The OCC lifted a 2022 consent order over the bank’s anti-money laundering controls in August 2025.

The bank no longer stands alone. Last December, the OCC granted conditional approvals to five more digital asset firms, including Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Paxos and Fidelity Digital Assets, to become national trust banks.

The asset manager is the latest in a run of expansions. On Nov. 5, Anchorage Digital Swap Dealer LLC applied to the National Futures Association to register as a swap dealer with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The company said much of its options growth has come from public companies holding bitcoin and ether on their balance sheets.

It has been revealed that in February, Tether made a $100 million strategic investment in Anchorage at a $4.2 billion valuation, after picking Anchorage Digital Bank as the issuer of its U.S. stablecoin. Anchorage also ran its first employee tender offer at that valuation instead of raising fresh primary capital.

In a recent development, in June, the company rolled out off-exchange settlement with Binance, letting institutions trade on the exchange while their assets stay in segregated custody at the bank. Anchorage also offers trading, staking and settlement to institutional clients.

The swap dealer application remains under review by the National Futures Association, and McCauley remarked at the time that the firm was not in a position to speculate on timing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Bitcoin put can cushion losses for its buyer, while the trades a dealer makes to hedge the same option can make a fresh selloff harder to stop.

In its Nov. 24 report, Glassnode estimated that options dealers could reinforce declines by selling and rallies by buying when Bitcoin traded between $58,000 and $64,000. The US inflation report due Nov. 25 gives that setup a near-term test.

On a seven-day average, 1.7 Bitcoin puts traded for every call, the highest ratio since June 2022, according to Glassnode’s Nov. 24 report.

In a recent development, the put-to-call ratio for outstanding contracts separately reached its highest since May 2021. Put trading includes sellers and positions that serve purposes beyond crash protection, so the volume ratio shows where activity shifted without revealing who took which side.

In a recent development, A put gives its buyer the right to sell at a fixed price, or receive the equivalent cash payoff. The lower Bitcoin finishes below that price, the larger the payoff before the option's cost.

In a recent development, A dealer who sells the put takes the other side of that exposure and can hedge by selling Bitcoin or futures. As Bitcoin falls, the put becomes more sensitive to the decline, and the dealer may need to sell more to keep the hedge balanced.

According to recent reports, gamma measures how swiftly an option’s price sensitivity changes. If prices reverse, a dealer in short gamma can buy back part of the hedge, adding to the rebound.

The feedback can be stronger when few buyers or sellers stand ready to take the other side, a pattern that researchers studying equity options found in less liquid stocks.

Recent findings suggest that glassnode estimated positive dealer gamma in the adjoining $56,000-$58,000 and $64,000-$66,000 bands. Dealers hedging positive gamma can buy weakness and sell strength, helping absorb a move. Those were modeled zones for one snapshot, and new trades or expiries can shift them.

A separate estimate from GEX Monitor from Nov. 24 also showed negative net gamma near $60,000, with the largest concentration by absolute exposure at that strike.

Glassnode’s Nov. 24 estimate put short gamma between $58,000 and $64,000. Bitcoin was near $59,700 later that day.

Within the estimated short-gamma band, dealer hedges can reinforce both a selloff and a rally.

It has been revealed that the bands describe an estimate at one point in time. Dealer positions, liquidity and the influence of hedging can change as prices move, trades arrive or contracts expire.

According to recent reports, range widths are proportional to the reported dollar spans. Glassnode’s estimates use Nov. 24 data at 16:00 UTC. The later CryptoSlate observation at 21:12 UTC is rounded to $59,700. The paths illustrate short-gamma dealers hedging a move.

The bands describe an estimate at one point in time. Dealer positions, liquidity and the influence of hedging can change as prices move, trades arrive or contracts expire.

It has been revealed that glassnode estimated that nearly 90% of the leveraged futures longs it had flagged between the prior week’s Bitcoin price and its realized price had cleared. Realized price is the average price at which coins last moved.

The selloff had already pushed into a $55,000-$62,000 cluster of positions at risk of liquidation.

Futures liquidations occur when traders can no longer meet their margin requirements, so options dealers rebalance as prices move even if nobody faces a margin call.

Glassnode reported $4.3 billion of net outflows from US spot Bitcoin ETFs over the 20 trading days covered in the report.

According to recent reports, the Bureau of Economic Analysis scheduled its October inflation report and revised third-quarter GDP for Nov. 25 at 8:30 a.m. ET. The inflation report includes the personal consumption expenditures price index (PCE).

In a recent development, trading Economics listed a 0.3% monthly consensus for core PCE, which excludes food and energy. The Cleveland Fed’s model estimated 0.27% separately.

Investors are watching what the data means for rates after the Fed’s October minutes indicated broad support for more tightening if the economy evolved as officials expected.

At derivatives exchange Deribit, Wednesday’s daily Bitcoin options are scheduled to expire at 3 a.m. ET, five and a half hours before the release.

They had about 6,172 BTC of open interest, around 1.4% of outstanding coin-settled Bitcoin options on Deribit, in Deribit’s Nov. 24 options data, against 111,797 BTC in the Nov. 27 monthly expiry.

Deribit’s Nov. 24 coin-settled Bitcoin options book showed 6,172 BTC of gross open interest in the daily expiry before PCE and 111,797 BTC in the monthly expiry after it. The exchange publishes open interest with an eight-hour lag.

Source: Deribit options data · Deribit expiry policy · Deribit public API changelog · BEA release schedule.

CryptoSlate estimated the effect of removing Wednesday’s expiry using coin-settled contracts expiring within 30 days.

According to recent reports, assuming dealers held the long side of every call and the short side of every put, contracts set to outlast the release accounted for about 93% of the Nov. 24 model’s net negative gamma.

The Nov. 27 expiry alone accounted for about 49% of the original total, leaving about 7% in Wednesday’s expiry under the same assumptions.

According to recent reports, the calculation holds prices and positions at their Nov. 24 readings, so actual gamma can shift as Bitcoin moves and expiry approaches, and the public exchange data counts contracts without identifying dealer positions.

The Nov. 27 put open interest was spread across several strikes, including $60,000, $63,000 and $64,000. At the same $60,000 strike, annualized implied volatility was 50.4% for Wednesday’s expiry, 56.1% for Thursday’s and 54.6% for Friday’s.

The higher Thursday and Friday marks cover the inflation release and other risks over longer periods.

A hot print could lift rate expectations and start a selloff that short-gamma dealers reinforce with hedge sales.

According to recent reports, A cool print could ease rate pressure and prompt a rebound that the same dealers reinforce by buying. If inflation comes in close to forecasts, the GDP figures and demand for Bitcoin could matter more.

According to recent reports, for the rest of the week, watch whether Friday’s expiry changes positioning and whether spot buyers return. The NYSE closes for Thanksgiving, ending Friday’s core equity session at 1 p.m. ET.

If dealers turn long gamma or liquidity improves enough to absorb their trades, the same catalyst could produce a smaller swing.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • They would have had to report those assets as of Dec.
  • This would have been the case even if they had held the same coins since January without making any sales.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, french senators on Nov. 24 rejected a proposal that would have required taxpayers to disclose self-hosted cryptocurrency holdings exceeding €100,000.

They would have had to report those assets as of Dec. 31.

This would have been the case even if they had held the same coins since January without making any sales.

Two matching amendments to the French 2027 budget were rejected by the Senate during the first reading of the draft.

Senators Pascal Savoldelli and Anne-Sophie Romagny reintroduced the proposal after it briefly passed in the National Assembly earlier in the month.

French taxpayers must disclose their crypto assets held on foreign crypto platforms.

These amendments would have expanded disclosure requirements to wallets that owners directly control. This pertains to a wallet that is not managed by an exchange or another custodian.

According to recent reports, the French National Assembly approved the €100,000 disclosure threshold in a 150-44 vote on Nov. 3. There were also eight abstentions.

The next day, the National Assembly voted down the entire revenue portion of the budget.

This vote brought down the wallet disclosure provision along with the rest of the budget.

However, the subsequent effort to revive the provision in the Senate was defeated.

It should be noted that the 2027 budget is still being considered at the time of writing.

The Senate also rejected two other crypto-related measures debated as part of the budget.

One was a provision to tax gains realized when holders exchange cryptocurrencies for certain stablecoins.

The second was a proposal to expand France's exit tax to include unrealized gains on cryptocurrencies held by taxpayers who move their tax residence outside the country.

#122442. Tech Report: Juiced Scrambler Mini debuted as a cooler (and safer) e-bike option for teens and parents

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1030 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Juiced Scrambler Mini debuted as a cooler (and safer) e-bike option for teens and parents

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1030 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Finding an electric bike for a teenager can be surprisingly tricky.
  • The newly launched Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.
  • The new youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding an electric bike for a teenager can be surprisingly tricky. Parents generally want something safe, manageable, and from a reputable company. Teenagers, meanwhile, generally want something that doesn’t look like it was picked out by their parents.

The newly launched Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.

The new youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm). But perhaps more importantly for parents, Juiced also built in a PIN-protected speed limiter known as Speed Lock that lets adults decide just how fast the bike can go.

In a recent development, the Scrambler Mini ships set to a 10 mph (16 km/h) Beginner Mode, but its maximum speed can be adjusted anywhere from 1-20 mph (32 km/h) and then locked behind a four-digit PIN. Juiced notes that riders aged 8-12 should not exceed 10 mph, while riders 13 and older can use the bike at speeds up to 20 mph, subject of course to local laws and regulations. In almost every state and jurisdiction though, the bike will fit Class 2 designation for street-legal riding and bike lane operation.

That setup seems like a pretty smart way to approach youth e-bikes. Instead of buying a slow bike that a teenager may quickly outgrow – or handing them a much faster machine before a parent thinks they’re ready – the same bike can essentially grow with the rider (with speed titrated by a parent or guardian).

And from the kid’s perspective, it certainly doesn’t look like a safety-first children’s bike.

The Scrambler Mini gets the same sort of moto-inspired styling that has defined Juiced’s Scrambler lineup, including a long bench seat, dual-crown-style fork, chunky 16 x 4-inch tires, and several appropriately loud color options including Blackberry, Fruit Punch, Blueberry, and Pink Lemonade.

Industry observers note that there’s some decent hardware underneath that styling, too. The rear hub motor is rated at 500W nominal and 1,092W peak with 80 Nm of torque. A removable 48V 10Ah battery using LG cells provides 480Wh of capacity, with Juiced claiming up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Four levels of cadence-based pedal assist are included, as is a right-side thumb throttle.

It has been revealed that the bike also features Talon hydraulic disc brakes with large 180mm rotors front and rear, 50mm of front suspension travel, an integrated backlit LCD, a headlight, and a rear taillight with brake-light functionality. The single-speed bike weighs 59 lb (26.8 kg), has a 27.15-inch seat height, and is rated for up to 275 lb (125 kg) of payload.

Those parts are far above what we normally see on e-bikes targeted towards teens, with most teen-focused e-bikes sporting cheaper components like mechanical brakes and rigid forks.

The Scrambler Mini is listed at $1,099, though Juiced is at the moment offering a Black Friday sale that drops the price by another $150 to just $949. The firm says preorders are expected to begin shipping the week of December 7.

Recent findings suggest that that price also comes with something increasingly important in the crowded youth e-bike market: an actual organization standing behind the bike. Juiced was founded in 2009, rapidly becoming a leader in the market for powerful and stylish e-bikes. But after the brand’s financial troubles a few years ago, Lectric eBikes stepped in to take Juiced under its wing in 2025. The relaunched Juiced now offers a three-year manufacturer warranty and US-based support, plus the peace of mind that comes with backing from North America’s largest e-bike company, Lectric eBikes.

That last part may be just as appealing to parents as the speed limiter, though the 3-year warranty is definitely a deal sweetener, too.

Recent findings suggest that there’s always going to be some controversy around the idea of e-bikes marketed towards teens, but I’m for it when done responsibly. Let’s face it: e-bikes are incredibly popular and teens are already going to be riding them, even if it means borrowing a friend’s e-bike because they don’t have their own. So if they’re going to be riding, the least we can do is put them on a safer, higher-quality bike so they learn the right skills in the right environment. And hey, it sure beats teens sitting alone in their rooms texting each other all afternoon.

It has been revealed that when it comes to choosing an e-bike, there are already plenty of cheap mini e-bikes and electric dirt bike-style machines floating around online, and many are undoubtedly going to look tempting to teenagers. The Scrambler Mini seems to take a different approach, giving young riders the styling, fat tires, throttle, and mini-moto attitude they actually want, while giving parents control over how much of that performance they can access.

It’s still an e-bike capable of 20 mph, and that means parents need to make decisions about where, when, and how their kids ride it. And there’s even an argument to be made for removing the throttle and turning it into a Class 1 e-bike in the beginning, requiring a teen to pedal it to engage the motor. But I’d much rather see that conversation happening around a bike with hydraulic brakes, lights, a programmable speed limit, and a real firm standing behind it than around some anonymous electric mini-bike bought from the depths of the internet.

And if the teenager thinks it looks cool enough to actually ride, that’s probably the point.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin exchange reserves have declined by approximately 42,000 BTC over the past month as the cryptocurrency struggles around $60,000.
  • The reduction comes as Bitcoin deposits and withdrawals across centralized trading platforms reached their highest levels since February, according to CryptoQuant data.
  • Exchange reserves fell from approximately 2.889 million BTC to 2.847 million BTC during a period in which Bitcoin's price declined roughly 26%, from $80,700 to $59,600.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin exchange reserves have declined by approximately 42,000 BTC over the past month as the cryptocurrency struggles around $60,000.

The reduction comes as Bitcoin deposits and withdrawals across centralized trading platforms reached their highest levels since February, according to CryptoQuant data.

Exchange reserves fell from approximately 2.889 million BTC to 2.847 million BTC during a period in which Bitcoin's price declined roughly 26%, from $80,700 to $59,600.

Sources indicate that the reduction approaches 50,000 BTC when measured from the Oct. 26 peak in exchange reserves.

Recent findings suggest that A Nov. 24 analysis by CryptoQuant contributor CryptoOnchain showed that daily Bitcoin deposits averaged 46,900 BTC over the seven days through Nov. 23, up 40.8% from the preceding week. Withdrawals increased even faster, rising 50.2% to 49,200 BTC daily.

Both figures reached their highest levels since Feb. 11, when Bitcoin traded near $67,048, approximately 9% above its Nov. 23 closing price of $61,195.

Bitcoin transfers through wallets tracked by CryptoQuant.

Withdrawals edged ahead even as deposits rose to a nine-month high.

Transfers between two tracked venues can count on both sides. The gross figures are rounded, and CryptoOnchain’s report does not list every venue.

Industry observers note that the gross bar adds CryptoOnchain’s rounded daily averages of 46,900 BTC in and 49,200 BTC out. The net bar uses its separately reported outflow of 2,369 BTC on the same scale. 2,369 divided by 96,100 is about 2.5%. All figures cover the seven days through Nov. 23, 2026.

It has been revealed that transfers between two tracked venues can count on both sides. The gross figures are rounded, and CryptoOnchain’s report does not list every venue.

According to recent reports, rising exchange deposits typically signal potential selling pressure, as investors move coins onto platforms where they can readily liquidate their holdings. Conversely, withdrawals can reduce the supply available for immediate sale.

The latest surge in activity left exchanges with average daily net withdrawals of 2,369 BTC, reversing estimated daily net inflows of roughly 550 BTC during the preceding week.

Binance accounted for approximately 60% of those net withdrawals, despite representing just 19% of combined exchange flows.

Meanwhile, CryptoQuant's exchange whale ratio, which measures the share of deposits attributable to the 10 largest inflows, declined 8.4% week over week to 22.52%.

The recent contraction in exchange reserves contrasts with the buildup that preceded Bitcoin's sharp decline earlier this month.

According to recent reports, between Nov. 8 and 11, exchange balances increased by approximately 15,000 BTC while Bitcoin traded between $74,000 and $75,000. The cryptocurrency subsequently fell to around $64,000.

Since Nov. 13, however, exchange reserves and Bitcoin's price have declined together, suggesting that existing exchange inventories may be supplying part of the market's selling pressure.

The latest surge in transfers also reflects potential changes in how Bitcoin is distributed across trading platforms.

As CryptoSlate previously reported, approximately 11,028 BTC moved from Coinbase- and Binance-linked addresses to Kraken on Nov. 21.

Such transfers can increase reported exchange activity without adding to aggregate reserves.

With fewer coins held across tracked exchanges, a recovery in demand could encounter a smaller pool of readily available Bitcoin.

However, exchange reserves have registered a modest increase over the past two days. Another buildup resembling the 15,000 BTC increase earlier this month could signal renewed selling pressure as Bitcoin attempts to defend $60,000.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Woodland version is bigger and more powerful than the standard Toyota bZ, and it may be a better deal right now.

Toyota now sells three electric SUVs in the US (see which one is the best fit for you): the bZ (previously called the bZ4Z), C-HR, and bZ Woodland.

The C-HR is a smaller, sportier crossover SUV, while the bZ Woodland adds a larger, more rugged option.

Toyota is presently offering a deal on the 2026 bZ Woodland for Black Friday that might be worth a look.

The deal includes 0% APR financing for 72 months, plus an extra $1,000 Holiday Bonus Cash. Toyota stated that if you finance a new 2026 bZ Woodland for 72 payments, it will cost $13.89 for every $1,000 financed.

In comparison, the standard 2026 bZ is available with 1.99% interest for 72 months at $14.75 for every $1,000 financed.

For leasing, the standard 2026 Toyota bZ is cheaper, starting at $369 per month. The deal is for a 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing for an effective cost of $490 per month.

Recent findings suggest that however, that’s for the single-motor FWD version. Upgrading to AWD will cost around $606 a month for the same 36-month lease with $4,369 due at signing.

Toyota is promoting 2026 bZ Woodland leases as low as $449 a month. That’s also for a 36-month lease with $4,448 due at signing.

The Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower, which is 37 hp more than the standard bZ SUV with AWD.

Toyota’s standard bZ is offered with FWD and AWD powertrains. FWD models deliver either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models produce a combined 338 hp.

The Woodland model is also 6″ longer than the standard bZ, opening up an additional 30 cubic feet of cargo space on the inside.

Toyota’s bigger SUV also adds a rugged look and off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and up to 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Other rugged upgrades are standard, including All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.

Inside, both come with a 7″ digital cluster and a large 14″ touchscreen running the latest Toyota Audio Multimedia system with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

Although it uses the same 74.7-kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland version offers slightly less driving range because of the added power and off-road equipment. The 2027 bZ Woodland has an estimated range of up to 281 miles with all-season tires, or 260 miles with the optional all-terrain tires.

Industry observers note that in comparison, the bZ is available with two battery packs: 57.7 kWh and 74.7 kWh. The base XLE FWD uses the 57.7 kWh battery, while the XLE AWD and FWD Plus, Limited AWD, and FWD models use the 74.7 kWh battery.

The standard 57.7 kWh battery provides an EPA range of up to 236 miles, while the 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 314 miles for FWD and 288 miles for AWD.

It has been revealed that both the bZ and bZ Woodland have a native NACS port, so drivers can use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. It takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

Scout Motors starts validation builds at $2B SC plant, deliveries in 2028

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1114 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars.
  • That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the organization was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.
  • According to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars. Scout confirms the first deliveries of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup won’t happen until 2028.

That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the organization was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.

According to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed. The Body Shop, Paint Shop, and Assembly Shop are all being used for the first validation builds.

Industry observers note that the Body Shop is the most automated part of the plant. Scout says more than 750 robots join roughly 160 parts into each body, laying down about 5,000 weld points per vehicle, with AI-supported weld monitoring and a metrology system checking the results. At full capacity, the shop is designed to handle about 40 vehicles per hour.

Bodies then go through an electrified paint shop before landing in final assembly, where they’re married to the chassis and get their wiring, glass, seats, and wheels.

CEO Scott Keogh is clearly happy to have something physical to point to, saying that “what we are building in Blythewood is no longer a promise on paper.”.

In a recent development, scout also shared photos of a Terra pickup and a Traveler parked inside the plant. Its own fine print notes that they show “concept and validation vehicles” with optional features, so don’t read too much into what’s on display:.

According to recent reports, fair enough. But Scout is also careful about what this stage is. Teams are confirming the equipment is installed and works, and checking engineering, buildability, and parts maturity. Process validation and scaling up to production speed come later. Validation builds will continue “into 2027,” followed by pre-production builds, and then customer deliveries in 2028.

The company claims the plant will create more than 4,000 jobs, and it’s spending another $300 million on an onsite supplier park expected to support about 1,000 supplier jobs.

Recent findings suggest that when Keogh laid out the blueprint in late 2023, Scout said it would start production in 2026 with deliveries shortly after. That was still the target when Scout broke ground in Blythewood in February 2024.

Sources indicate that by the Traveler and Terra unveiling in October 2024, production had moved to 2027. Keogh then said in March that he expects the first customer to get a vehicle “sometime in 2028,” and that’s now the official line in Scout’s own press materials.

It has been revealed that it might not even be the end of it. Industry forecaster AutoForecast Solutions has the Traveler starting production in September 2028 and the Terra in March 2030. Scout hasn’t confirmed those dates, but it hasn’t given more precise ones either.

The product itself has also changed under the hood. Scout launched as a pure EV brand, then added the “Harvester” range-extender option at the reveal. According to Keogh, Scout has more than 160,000 reservations, and 87% of them are for the gas-generator version. Those are $100 refundable reservations, not orders.

Der Spiegel reported earlier this year that integrating the range extender, which wasn’t part of the original plan, was among the technical problems pushing the timeline back.

Industry observers note that for comparison, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and delivered the first ones four years later, a delay that was widely mocked. Scout is now on a similar four-year path from reveal to customer, and that’s for the SUV it’s launching first.

A working body shop with 750 robots isn’t vaporware. Scout has a real factory, a real workforce, and two vehicles that people clearly want. 160,000 reservations is a big number for a brand that hasn’t sold a single vehicle in 46 years.

Industry observers note that but validation builds are an early step, not a finish line. Scout still has to go through pre-production, prove its processes, and ramp to rate, and every one of those stages is where new automakers usually lose time. Rivian and Lucid both learned that the hard way.

Sources indicate that september 28? So we're 23 months away? I'm surprised the validation build yadda yadda stuff is supposed to take so long. It's not like VW doesn't know how to do this stuff, and that's a lot of money and equipment to sit mostly idle while 180,000 reservations holders are waiting for their cars. Maybe they're waiting for the market to change or are considering a whole other brand or product line?

In a recent development, and the market Scout was designed for in 2022 no longer exists. The EV tax credit is gone, and most of Scout’s own reservation holders picked the gas generator. In the US, the range-extender market is still early, unlike in China, where they are already popular.

Industry observers note that but by 2028, Ford, Ram, and Jeep all strategy to have range-extended trucks and SUVs on sale. Scout’s main advantage was being early with a cool, rugged, American-built electric truck. That advantage shrinks every quarter.

We’re still rooting for these vehicles. The Traveler and Terra are among the best-looking designs in the segment. But a $100 reservation is easy to walk away from, and the question is how many of those 160,000 people are still waiting in 2028.
